The original cargo Manatee carries up to 1,044 tons of cargo in open bays situated on a single deck. This straightforward layout, which would later prove ideal for BattleMech gantry installation, provides efficient loading and unloading through individual bay doors. The vessel carries no offensive or defensive weaponry whatsoever, relying entirely on escort vessels or fighter screens for protection during transit.

A crew of just six personnel operates the vessel, making it one of the most economical DropShips to crew in the Inner Sphere. One hundred seven single heat sinks manage the drive system's thermal output. Safe thrust of 4g provides adequate performance for a cargo vessel, while 280 points of armor offer basic protection against micrometeorites and incidental damage. The Manatee's compact 37-meter length and robust systems make it easy to maintain, contributing to its extraordinary longevity as a design.

The invention of the BattleMech changed the face of warfare, but the limiting factor for military planners was not how many BattleMechs they could build, but how to transport them from jump point to planetary surface. Early attempts to use existing military vehicle or infantry transports demonstrated limited success. The Terran Hegemony Naval Department began experimenting with converting merchant cargo hulls into military BattleMech haulers, and the Manatee's open cargo bays on a single deck made it the most promising candidate.

The Manatee's first BattleMech deployment came on Kentares in 2449, where Hegemony forces faced Davion's Fourth Avalon Hussars. Initially the BattleMechs proved their worth, but the Hussars discovered the Manatee was too lightly armed and armored, and began targeting the transports directly. Several DropShips and their precious BattleMechs were lost, forcing the Hegemony to deploy heavier fighter screens. The BattleMech-carrying Manatee was soon retired from frontline service, though the concept it proved led directly to purpose-built BattleMech carriers.

The basic cargo Manatee was eventually copied by other Inner Sphere powers, with Periphery variants appearing during the Reunification War. Thought extinct by the collapse of the First Star League, the Manatee was rediscovered in service with Nueva Castile in the Deep Periphery. By 3080, Bordello Military Goods, Inc. in Antwerp continued building the design, ensuring the oldest BattleMech-associated DropShip remained in production millennia after its introduction.

The Merlin class assault DropShip is a combination WarShip escort and fast-attack craft developed through collaboration between the Free Worlds League and its allies in the early 3060s. This 2,500-ton Spheroid was created to fill a gap in the League's naval capabilities after the collapse of an alliance that had previously provided access to comparable assault craft production.

Rushed through design and testing, the Merlin proved surprisingly well-rounded despite its expedited development. Fast, well-armored, and carrying substantial firepower, the design earned rave reviews from crews and the vessels it was assigned to protect. Its primary limitations are minor heat management issues and a restricted fuel supply that demands careful planning during independent operations.

The Merlin was born from the Word of Blake-Free Worlds League alliance, intended to replace the Capellan Lung Wang assault craft that had become unavailable following the collapse of the Marik-Liao pact. With Word of Blake technical assistance, the design process was expedited and the first Merlin entered service in 3063. Despite being rushed into production, the design exhibited remarkably few flaws.

Irian Technologies' Clipperton facility assembled more than a dozen Merlins by 3067, while the Brigadier Corporation's Gibson plant suffered a series of manufacturing accidents that limited its output to a single vessel and consumed excessive materials. Word of Blake security forces traced these problems to ComStar saboteurs and expected the plant to reach full efficiency shortly thereafter.

During the Jihad, a unique Merlin was captured from the Word of Blake and refitted into a pocket WarShip configuration by the Principality of Regulus. This success led to a limited production variant, though output remained low as the Principality had to acquire standard Merlins and convert them individually. The Merlin has remained in service with most of the former and reconstituted Free Worlds League powers and various mercenary forces into the thirty-second century.

The Mówáng-class Courier is a compact civilian Small Craft conceived during the early First Succession War to serve the personal transport needs of Capellan Confederation nobility. Commissioned by the House of Scions in 2835, the design was built around simplicity, passenger comfort, and low production cost. The House declared an open manufacturing license immediately upon introduction, inviting any world with adequate industrial capacity to build the craft without restriction. That decision spread the Mówáng across dozens of systems within a few generations, making it among the most widely distributed personal spacecraft in the Inner Sphere. Lightly built and unarmed, the vessel relies on its mundane appearance and near-universal familiarity to pass scrutiny wherever it operates.

The Mówáng is a 100-ton Civilian Aerodyne Small Craft powered by a standard fusion powerplant delivering a safe thrust of 4G and a maximum thrust of 6G, providing adequate performance for intra-system transit between planetary surfaces, orbital stations, and jump points. Fuel capacity supports routine system hops without requiring intermediate resupply. The craft's three-man crew is drawn from the employing noble's personal staff, valued for discretion rather than combat experience.

Passenger accommodations are modest but well-appointed for a vessel of this class. A single first-class stateroom serves the primary passenger, while two steerage-rated cabins accommodate aides or companions. Cargo capacity is limited to five and a half tons, accessed through a single cargo door, which is sufficient for personal effects, gifts, or contraband at the owner's discretion.

Armor protection amounts to just two and a half tons of standard plating, arranged to deflect debris rather than withstand weapons fire. The Mówáng carries no armament whatsoever. These limitations reflect deliberate design choices: military protection would raise costs and attract inspection. The craft's entire defensive strategy rests on appearing unremarkable. Its construction is intentionally within the manufacturing capability of any modestly industrialized world, which is reflected in its price tag of roughly 3.5 million C-bills.

The Mówáng-class Courier emerged in the early years of the First Succession War, when established DropShip service networks grew unreliable and Capellan nobles sought alternatives for private intra-system travel. The House of Scions, the aristocratic body overseeing Capellan nobility, sponsored the design with specific requirements: the craft had to be affordable, simple to build, and comfortable enough for a Diem to use as a personal vehicle. The open manufacturing license declared in 2835 was a deliberate policy choice, intended to maximize production across the Confederation's many worlds rather than concentrate output at a handful of licensed facilities. Within decades, the design had spread throughout the Capellan Confederation and was being produced by local manufacturers on dozens of worlds.

Throughout the Succession Wars the Mówáng occupied a quiet but persistent niche. Capellan Diems used them to travel between worlds in their multi-planetary holdings, convey valuables, and move goods, licit or otherwise, beyond the reach of formal customs networks. Their unremarkable profile meant that military and customs patrols rarely subjected them to serious scrutiny. As the design spread beyond the Confederation, nobles and wealthy merchants in neighboring states acquired them for the same reasons. By the time of the Clan Invasion, the Mówáng had become common enough in Inner Sphere system traffic that a single craft could move through most ports without comment.

That anonymity proved dangerous during the Jihad. In 3073, the Word of Blake acquired a number of Mówáng hulls provided by Kali Liao and modified them as covert assault transports. The conversions stripped out passenger quarters, installed battle armor bays capable of carrying two Level Is of troops, reduced the engine output to free internal volume, increased armor protection to four tons, and fitted an Angel ECM suite. The modified craft were used as clandestine insertion vehicles, exploiting the Mówáng's civilian identity to approach targets aboard passenger DropShips or JumpShips before executing attack runs. Most of these converted hulls were destroyed or captured before the Jihad concluded, but the episode left a residual wariness. Several jurisdictions instituted enhanced inspection requirements for Mówáng-type craft in the early Republic era, and the vessel's reputation as an innocent courier was never fully restored.

The Mule class DropShip is one of the most common civilian vessels in known space, a ubiquitous spheroid cargo transport encountered on virtually every trade route across the Inner Sphere. Designed during the height of the Star League in 2737, the Mule has endured for centuries thanks to its practical and uncomplicated design, affordability, ease of maintenance, and surprisingly spacious crew accommodations. These qualities make the Mule highly attractive to independent traders and small shipping firms, ensuring its continued production long after more sophisticated Star League-era designs fell out of use.

At 11,200 tons, the Mule carries a generous amount of armor and weaponry for a merchant vessel, boasting an arsenal that rivals those of some small military DropShips. Its cargo capacity of nearly 8,500 tons and versatile interior layout have made it the standard by which all other civilian freighters are measured.

The Mule entered production in 2737, during the final decades of the Star League when interstellar trade volume was at its historical peak. The design filled a critical niche between smaller cargo shuttles and the enormous Mammoth class, offering substantial hauling capacity at a price point accessible to independent operators and mid-sized shipping firms. The Mule quickly became the most popular civilian cargo carrier in the Inner Sphere, a status it would maintain through centuries of conflict and upheaval.

The Star League's collapse and the onset of the Succession Wars tested the Mule's durability in ways its designers never anticipated. While more complex military vessels became irreplaceable casualties of the conflicts, the Mule's straightforward engineering and widely available components ensured that production could continue even as the Inner Sphere's technological base deteriorated. The drive system proved so reliable and well-understood that it was adapted for use in the Excalibur class military transport when that vessel's original propulsion supply dwindled, further cementing the Mule's importance to the Inner Sphere's industrial base.

Plans for a comprehensive refit incorporating recovered Star League technology were under consideration by the early 3050s, but the arrival of the Clans and the resulting demand for military DropShip production delayed any upgrades indefinitely. The Mule continued in its original configuration, its proven reliability valued more than ever during a period of heightened military tension. Clan merchants adopted a variant designated the Mule C, incorporating minor modifications suited to Clan production methods while preserving the fundamental design.

The Word of Blake's Jihad saw the Mule pressed into an entirely new role when Blakist engineers converted several hulls into Pocket WarShip configurations, mounting capital missile launchers and fighter bays in place of cargo holds. These weaponized Mules, including the deceptive Q-Ship variant that retained civilian-grade armor to maintain the appearance of a harmless freighter, represented a dramatic departure from the vessel's peaceful origins. Following the Jihad, the Mule returned to its traditional role, remaining in production at facilities across the Inner Sphere well into the thirty-second century.

The Pentagon is a 4,000-ton Spheroid assault DropShip originally designed for the Terran Hegemony Navy as a dedicated anti-fighter escort for capital warships. First introduced in the mid-twenty-sixth century, the vessel was designed to generate acceleration exceeding five gravities, making it faster than virtually any other DropShip of its era and capable of matching the pace of most aerospace fighters over extended distances.

Heavily armed and exceptionally well-armored for its size, the Pentagon earned a fearsome reputation as one of the most dangerous combat DropShips ever fielded. Its weapons were regularly updated with the best technology available, ensuring the design remained lethal across multiple centuries of service with the Star League Defense Force and its successors.

The original Pentagon Mk I mounts a devastating array of conventional weaponry distributed across all firing arcs. The nose concentrates two LRM-20 racks, two PPCs, two large lasers, and two AC/10 autocannons. Each broadside carries an even heavier loadout: two forward-facing LRM-20s, two PPCs, a large laser, and four medium lasers, plus an aft-facing PPC, LRM-20, AC/10, and two large lasers. The stern mounts a large laser, four medium lasers, and a PPC for rear defense.

One hundred seventy single heat sinks manage the considerable thermal load. Over seventy-five tons of armor provide 1,292 points of protection, exceptional for a vessel of this size. The GM 5600 Sublite maneuver drives generate 5.573g of thrust, pushing crews to the very limits of human endurance. A crew of fifty-five operates the vessel, which carries 594 tons of cargo including ammunition stores for its ballistic weapons.

The Pentagon was first designed for the Terran Hegemony Navy in the twenty-sixth century to provide anti-fighter escort for Congress-class Frigates. In the years following the Reunification War, SLDF WarShips were rarely called into action against other capital vessels, and with growing demand for convoy escorts, the Congress-class and their attached Pentagons often saw more action than the SLDF's battlecruiser and battleship squadrons combined.

During the Second Periphery Uprising, the SLS Star Devil, a Congress-class frigate, stumbled into four aging Taurian Lola II destroyers screening a force bound for Brisbane. Far from any support, the Star Devil launched both her Pentagons with orders to concentrate on the Taurian troop transports. Fighting through the enemy fighter screen, the DropShips inflicted crippling damage on four JumpShips before being destroyed. The Star Devil was also lost, but not before taking three enemy destroyers with her.

The automated Caspar defense drones protecting the Terran Hegemony treated Pentagons as high-priority targets, and none are recorded as surviving the campaign to retake Terra from the Usurper. The design was thought extinct until 3068, when ComStar's Case White assault on Terra encountered previously unknown Word of Blake naval units including several squadrons of Pentagons. The Word of Blake had secretly developed a modified variant mounting capital-grade missile launchers, transforming the already dangerous escort into a pocket warship capable of engaging capital vessels directly.

The Princess class luxury liner is an 11,800-ton Spheroid DropShip produced by the Nicholas Spacecraft Company of New Earth for the Terran Hegemony beginning in 2657. Designed as the ultimate expression of civilian luxury in interstellar travel, the Princess surpassed even the celebrated Monarch class in passenger amenities during the Star League era. Twice the size of the Monarch, the vessel featured unmatched accommodations including a simulated terrestrial garden, swimming pool, wine lockers, and round-the-clock servant staff.

The Princess was extraordinarily expensive to operate even during the height of the Star League. Over centuries of service under various owners, many of the high-maintenance luxury features were progressively removed in favor of additional passenger or cargo capacity, with some vessels being fully converted to bulk freighters.

The cargo refit variant strips all luxury and specialty decks from the original Princess design, converting the entire interior to bulk cargo hauling. The former swimming pool deck becomes a liquid cargo bay, the simulated terrestrial garden deck is replaced with a standard cargo hold, and remaining passenger spaces are expanded into additional cargo bays. Total cargo capacity reaches 4,795 tons, more than tripling the original configuration's freight capability. The crew complement is reduced from 354 to 176 personnel with the elimination of hospitality staff.

The defensive armament remains unchanged from the original design: a nose-mounted large laser with two machine guns, two medium lasers with four machine guns per broadside, and an aft medium laser with two machine guns. Sixty single heat sinks manage the modest thermal output. Four small craft bays are retained for utility operations. The vessel's armor protection of 312 points and safe thrust of three reflect the original civilian design priorities, with minimal defensive capability appropriate for a vessel never intended for combat operations.

The Princess class was introduced in 2657 by the Nicholas Spacecraft Company of New Earth, quickly becoming the premier luxury passenger vessel of the Star League era. However, the design's extreme operating costs limited production numbers even during peacetime. The main shipyard producing the Princess was destroyed in 2805 during the Succession Wars, dealing a severe blow to the class's future.

Nicholas Spacecraft had previously licensed the design to Majesty Metals and Manufacturing in the Magistracy of Canopus. Although Majesty Metals also lost the capacity to build new Princess vessels, they retained the ability to maintain the few remaining examples in service with Magistracy fleets, preserving their original ultra-luxurious configurations. By 3067, Majesty Metals indicated that limited production of the Princess might resume, and as of 3143, newly constructed examples were reportedly being produced by the company. Most surviving Princess vessels outside the Magistracy had long since been stripped of their luxury amenities and converted to cargo haulers, a pragmatic but ignoble fate for what had once been the finest passenger vessel in known space.

The Seeker is a 4,700-ton Spheroid troop transport designed to carry a scout battalion into hostile territory and operate independently of support vessels for extended periods. Introduced in 2815 during the early Succession Wars, the design prioritizes speed, endurance, and crew comfort over raw firepower, reflecting its intended role as a deep reconnaissance platform rather than a front-line assault ship.

One of the fastest DropShips of its size class, the Seeker carries enough parts, food, and water to operate for up to four months without resupply. Relatively luxurious crew quarters and an extensive medical facility promote morale during lengthy independent deployments, making the design popular with scout commands and reconnaissance units across multiple Successor States.

The Seeker entered service in 2815 and was produced by multiple manufacturers across the Inner Sphere, ensuring widespread availability throughout the Succession Wars. The design's combination of speed, endurance, and versatile transport capacity made it a staple of scout and reconnaissance formations in every major military. Its reconfigurable cargo bays allowed field commanders to tailor the vessel's loadout to mission requirements, carrying light vehicles, BattleMechs, or even aerospace fighters as needed.

Refitted versions of the Seeker appeared following the rediscovery of Star League technology. The most common upgrade was jointly developed by Semier Data Tron and Salvatore Inc. for the Federated Commonwealth in 3054, incorporating extended-range energy weapons and improved fire control systems. Both the Free Worlds League and the Capellan Confederation were also reported to be developing their own upgraded variants, though these programs were not publicly confirmed. The Seeker has remained in continuous service across the Inner Sphere, its proven reliability and adaptable design ensuring relevance well beyond its original era.

The ST-46 Shuttle is the most common general-purpose shuttlecraft operating across the Inner Sphere and Periphery. Introduced in 2528, seventy years before the more specialized KR-61 Long-Range Shuttlecraft, the ST-46 became the standard short-hop utility craft for JumpShips, WarShips, space stations, and large transports throughout known space. Designed for reliability and versatility over passenger comfort or long-range endurance, it filled a niche no other single vessel could claim as broadly as its own.

The Vampire is one of the smallest DropShips ever to see combat, a tiny 400-ton Aerodyne so fast and well-armed that it is frequently mistaken for a heavy aerospace fighter. Conceived as the fastest jump infantry carrier in existence, the Vampire was designed to minimize the time its embarked troops were exposed to enemy interceptors by matching the performance of non-interceptor fighters it might encounter.

The vessel's distinctive combat profile involves high-speed, low-altitude passes over targets, during which jump infantry deploy through specialized ventral drop hatches. At long range, this gives the Vampire the appearance of a fighter on a bombing run, a deliberate deception that has proven highly effective at sowing confusion among defenders expecting ordnance rather than infantry. This combination of speed, firepower, and tactical surprise has made the Vampire a prized asset for special operations forces.

The Vampire II is a heavier 600-ton variant created specifically for battle armor infantry deployment. The design replaces the original's jump infantry compartments with four Battle Armor bays and eight tons of cargo. The weapons suite is entirely energy-based, eliminating ammunition dependency. Four Heavy PPCs mounted in the nose provide devastating long-range firepower, while each wing carries two Large X-Pulse Lasers and two Laser Anti-Missile Systems for close defense. The aft arc mounts two ER large lasers.

Communications equipment in the hull supports coordination with deployed battle armor forces. With ninety-four double heat sinks managing the all-energy weapons load, the Vampire II can sustain fire effectively. The vessel's safe thrust of four is lower than the original's six, reflecting the increased mass, but 565 points of armor provide substantially greater protection. A crew of forty-eight operates the vessel.

The Vampire was developed by Markesan Astronautics for the Federated Suns, entering service in 2715 as a specialized jump infantry delivery platform. The design proved highly effective during the Border War between the Federated Suns and the Capellan Confederation, where defending troops were thrown into confusion when jump infantry began raining down from what they assumed were fighter bombing runs. Federated Suns Special Forces became particularly fond of the Vampire for its ability to achieve tactical surprise.

However, the Vampire's high performance came at a significant cost. Its powerful drive system had a relatively short operational lifespan and required maintenance far exceeding that of comparable DropShip engines. When Markesan Astronautics' manufacturing facilities were destroyed during the Draconis Combine's First Succession War thrust toward New Avalon, the several dozen surviving Vampires were gradually grounded and eventually scrapped as their engines failed without replacement parts available.

The design was considered lost until the recovery of the Hegemony Memory Core during the Jihad enabled Jalastar Aerospace to revive the Vampire. The company began producing updated versions for the AFFS's special forces, incorporating modern weapons technology while retaining the original design's core philosophy of speed and deception. Subsequent variants expanded the concept to include battle armor delivery alongside the traditional jump infantry role.

The Vengeance class is the largest dedicated aerospace fighter carrier in common use among the Successor States. Introduced in 2682 during the height of the Star League, this 11,400-ton Aerodyne was designed to serve as a mobile fighter base capable of deploying up to forty aerospace fighters in support of fleet operations. Manufactured by Kallon Industries, Salvatore Incorporated, and Tomori Trans Industrial, the Vengeance earned a reputation as a critical strategic asset wherever it deployed.

Its distinctive flat, boxy hull spreads across forty-seven relatively compact decks rather than the large open cargo spaces found on most DropShips. Despite its Aerodyne classification, the broad profile prevents atmospheric operations, limiting the vessel to space-based deployments. This restriction has never diminished its value, as the fighter wings it commands can project power across an entire star system, making the Vengeance one of the most sought-after carrier designs in the Inner Sphere.

The Vengeance class fighter carrier entered service in 2682, during the final decades of the Star League. Designed to serve as a dedicated mobile fighter base, the Vengeance could deploy an entire aerospace fighter regiment from a single vessel. Three manufacturers produced the design: Kallon Industries, Salvatore Incorporated, and Tomori Trans Industrial, ensuring widespread distribution across the Star League Defense Force and member state navies.

The Succession Wars devastated Vengeance fleets across the Inner Sphere. As a high-priority target, the carrier attracted concentrated attacks that its relatively thin armor struggled to withstand. The loss of advanced manufacturing capability during the wars forced all three production lines to simplify components, and replacement vessels could not keep pace with attrition. By the end of the Third Succession War, functioning Vengeance carriers had become prized strategic assets, with some Successor States resorting to cannibalization of damaged hulls to keep their remaining carriers operational.

The recovery of Star League-era technology following the Helm Memory Core's rediscovery enabled significant upgrades to the Vengeance design. The 3056 refit introduced upgraded energy weapons, an advanced ballistic weapon in the nose, and enhanced missile tracking systems across all batteries. These improvements addressed the original design's chief weakness in engagement range while freeing tonnage for additional cargo capacity and maintaining the vessel's core identity as a fighter platform.

The Jihad-era arms race prompted the Magistracy of Canopus to develop a Vengeance Pocket WarShip conversion. This radical redesign halved the fighter complement, replacing bays with sub-capital weaponry, expanded missile armament, defensive countermeasures, and infantry quarters for boarding operations. The prototype, designated the Danai Centrella in honor of the Magistrix, demonstrated the viability of converting existing carrier hulls into sub-capital combatants. The production DC variant refined this concept, optimizing the weapons layout and reducing crew requirements through increased automation.

The Vengeance continues to serve in naval forces across the Inner Sphere and Periphery. Its enduring value lies not in its own armament but in the devastating power of the fighter wing it deploys, making the Vengeance a force multiplier that remains relevant from the Star League through the Dark Age.

production.manufacturer: Lockheed/CBM Corp.

text.overview: The Lockheed/CBM LC-100 Astrolux StarYacht is the most popular long-range civilian spacecraft designed for private ownership in the Inner Sphere. Produced at Lockheed/CBM's Donegal facilities, it has been the defining craft of its category since its introduction in 2953.
text.capabilities: The LC-100 carries fuel sufficient for more than a week of travel at 1G and food stores for a month of sustained space travel. Luxury quarters accommodate seven passengers, and a five-ton cargo bay handles personal freight. The Astrolux can land in the small craft bay of any DropShip or JumpShip as easily as at a planetary port, making it suitable for complex multi-leg voyages.
text.battleHistory: Introduced in 2953, the Astrolux's combination of range, comfort, and versatility prompted numerous knock-off designs and legal disputes over the following century. Despite that competition, the LC-100 remains one of Lockheed/CBM's most successful civilian products.

production.manufacturer: Galileo Instruments

text.capabilities:
The Achilles is built around its enormous Xevex-12 drive system, which accounts for over half the vessel's total mass and delivers up to six gravities of acceleration. This extraordinary thrust-to-weight ratio allows the Achilles to outmaneuver most heavy fighters and DropShips alike. However, thrust levels above four gravities produce intense vibrations that stress the ship's mechanical systems, particularly the ammunition feeds for its autocannon and missile batteries. Prolonged high-thrust flight can cause serious damage to both crew and vessel, making sustained maximum performance a calculated risk rather than standard operating procedure.

Lacking wings or lifting surfaces of any kind, the Achilles operates exclusively in space. Its weapons array spans all firing arcs, mounting six PPCs, three AC/20s, two AC/10s, four AC/5s, six LRM-20 racks, an LRM-10, four large lasers, and twelve medium lasers. The original model carries 124 single heat sinks to manage this considerable firepower. A platoon of thirty marines is housed in dedicated barracks amidships, deploying via a pair of combat buses carried in the aft small craft bays. Two additional bays house aerospace fighters that provide escort or conduct strike operations during fleet engagements.
text.deployment: The original Achilles entered service with the SLDF in 2582 and was rapidly adopted by every Great House military. Common tactical doctrine placed the Achilles at the head of planetary assault formations, with fighter escorts striking first to distract defenders or following behind to destroy survivors. The design saw extensive service throughout the Star League era and continued in diminishing numbers through the Succession Wars, with the Draconis Combine maintaining the largest surviving fleet thanks to its control of the Schuyler production facility.

production.manufacturer: Galileo Instruments|O'Neil Yards - Titan Yards|Rashpur-Owens Inc.

text.capabilities:
The Capellan-built (3055) variant represented a significant technological upgrade over the original design. All standard heat sinks were replaced with doubles, and the energy weapons suite was comprehensively modernized with extended-range PPCs and large lasers replacing the originals. Medium pulse lasers supplanted the standard medium lasers, providing improved accuracy at close range. Each LRM rack received an Artemis IV fire control system, substantially increasing missile accuracy against maneuvering targets.

Structural integrity was improved to 17, making the (3055) variant slightly more resilient to critical damage than its predecessors. Six escape pods replaced the original four, improving crew survivability. The small craft bays and marine complement were retained, preserving the boarding assault role. Cargo capacity was reduced slightly to 122 tons to accommodate the upgraded weapons and electronics.
text.deployment: The (3055) variant emerged from Rashpur-Owens Incorporated facilities above Capella in 3055, marking the unexpected return of Achilles production outside the Draconis Combine. These Capellan-built vessels deployed alongside the new Kuan Ti and Lung Wang DropShips as part of a broader naval modernization program. Despite their relatively small numbers, the upgraded Capellan Achilles proved formidable enough to alter the naval balance in the Capellan March.

production.manufacturer: Alshain Naval Yards (Civilian)|Krester Ship Construction|Krester Ship Construction|Krester Ship Construction|Krester Ship Construction

text.overview: The Aqueduct Liquid Carrier is a specialized civilian DropShip designed for the bulk transport of liquid cargo between worlds. Purpose-built to carry water, fuel, and other essential liquids to colonies and industrial installations lacking local supplies, the Aqueduct fills a critical but unglamorous niche in interstellar commerce. The design has been produced by multiple manufacturers across the Inner Sphere, reflecting the universal demand for reliable liquid transport capacity. While lacking the prestige of military vessels or passenger liners, the Aqueduct has earned a reputation as a dependable workhorse among merchant fleets and colonial support operations.
text.capabilities: The Aqueduct is a civilian spheroid DropShip optimized entirely for liquid cargo transport. Its hull is dominated by sealed storage tanks designed to carry water, industrial chemicals, fuel, or other liquid commodities in bulk quantities. The vessel mounts only minimal defensive armament, reflecting its purely commercial role and the expectation that it will operate along established trade routes or under military escort when venturing into contested space. Armor protection is correspondingly light, sufficient to ward off opportunistic pirate attacks but inadequate against determined military opposition. The Aqueduct's drive system provides modest acceleration typical of civilian transports, prioritizing fuel efficiency and operational range over speed. Internal systems include specialized pumping equipment, environmental controls to maintain cargo at required temperatures, and contamination prevention measures that allow the vessel to carry potable water and hazardous chemicals in separate tank systems during the same voyage. The design's emphasis on reliability over performance has proven well-suited to its role, with individual ships often serving for decades with minimal refit requirements.
text.deployment: The standard Aqueduct serves in its baseline liquid cargo carrier configuration, transporting water, fuel, and industrial chemicals between worlds. These vessels are most commonly found supporting colonial development operations, orbital construction projects, and military supply chains where bulk liquid transport is required.
text.battleHistory:
The Aqueduct emerged from the practical necessity of supporting human expansion across the stars. As colonies spread beyond worlds with readily accessible water supplies, the need for dedicated liquid transport vessels became acute. Early attempts to convert standard cargo DropShips for liquid carriage proved inefficient, prompting the development of a purpose-built design with integrated tank systems and specialized handling equipment.

Multiple manufacturers across the Inner Sphere have produced the Aqueduct over the centuries, with production driven by regional demand rather than centralized military procurement. The design has seen periodic updates to its systems and construction standards, but its fundamental layout has remained largely unchanged, evidence of the soundness of the original concept. During the Succession Wars, Aqueducts became critical military assets despite their civilian origins, as armies discovered that controlling water supplies could be as strategically decisive as controlling territory.

The Jihad disrupted many established trade routes, increasing demand for Aqueducts capable of reaching isolated worlds cut off from regular commerce. In the post-Jihad era, the design continues to serve across all major factions, with no single power able to claim a monopoly on production or operation.

production.manufacturer: Rumiko Yards|United Outworlders Corporation

text.capabilities:
The Arcadia mounts an impressive arsenal of advanced Clan weaponry across all firing arcs, taking full advantage of the newest technology available. The nose concentrates four Heavy Large Lasers, five Heavy Medium Lasers, and a pair of ATM-12 launchers, providing devastating firepower at multiple range bands. Each broadside carries three Heavy Large Lasers, five Heavy Medium Lasers, two Ultra AC/20s, and two ATM-9 racks. The aft arc is defended by five Heavy Medium Lasers and three Streak SRM-6 launchers. Two hundred fourteen double heat sinks manage the substantial thermal output of this weapons suite.

The vessel carries bay space for three Points of ProtoMechs along with nearly two hundred tons of cargo capacity. A crew of one hundred fourteen operates the vessel. With a safe thrust of six and structural integrity of eleven, the Arcadia matches or exceeds the maneuverability of most Clan aerospace fighters while carrying armor protection totaling over a thousand points across all arcs.
text.deployment: The original Arcadia entered service exclusively with Clan Blood Spirit in 3066, operating from their limited holdings in the Clan Homeworlds. These vessels were employed to prosecute Trials of Possession against neighboring Clans, delivering ProtoMech forces to contested objectives with speed and precision. The Arcadia's exceptional agility allowed Blood Spirit commanders to choose their engagements carefully, avoiding unfavorable encounters with superior naval forces while striking at objectives of opportunity.

production.manufacturer: United Outworlders Corporation

text.capabilities:
The 3080 refit of the Arcadia reduces ProtoMech capacity to a single Point while adding two Battle Armor bays capable of carrying two Points of armored infantry. Cargo capacity increases to over two hundred twenty tons. The weapons array has been significantly reworked, replacing the Ultra AC/20s and ATM-12 launchers with four HAG/40 hyper-assault Gauss rifles distributed across the broadsides and six ATM-9 launchers covering the flanks and aft arcs. The most notable addition is a pair of Manta Ray sub-capital missile launchers mounted in the nose, giving the vessel limited anti-WarShip capability.

The refit retains ten Heavy Large Lasers and twenty Heavy Medium Lasers across all arcs. The crew complement drops substantially to sixty-eight, reflecting increased automation. Armor protection, thrust performance, and heat sink capacity remain identical to the original configuration.
text.deployment: The 3080 refit emerged during the tumultuous Wars of Reaving that ravaged the Clan Homeworlds. The addition of sub-capital missile launchers and Battle Armor bays suggests a shift in operational doctrine toward anti-WarShip and boarding operations. The fate of any refitted Arcadia vessels, like that of their parent Clan, remains unknown following the isolation of the Homeworld Clans from the Inner Sphere.

text.overview: The Ares Assault Craft represents the combat-hardened branch of the Ares small craft lineage, tracing its origins to the primitive Mk.III of 2451 and evolving into the Mark VII, one of the most widely produced military landing craft in the Inner Sphere. Developed by IncStar Dynamics as a dedicated fighter-engagement variant, the Mk.III prioritized combat capability while retaining limited cargo capacity. Its heavier engine and upgraded armor set a template that later designers refined during the Succession Wars into the standard-technology Mark VII, produced at multiple factories and fielded by every major Inner Sphere power. The Clan adaptation, designated the Mark VII-C, brought advanced Clan technology to the same proven airframe, completing the long evolution from a primitive Age of War design into a craft that would serve in front-line roles across the entire Inner Sphere and Clan space well into the ilClan era.
text.capabilities:
The Mk.III Assault Craft substantially upgrades both propulsion and protection over the base Ares design. Its more powerful primitive fusion engine nearly doubles the maximum thrust of the Mk.I, allowing the craft to pursue and intercept enemy fighters rather than simply defend. Heavier armor and additional heat sinks reflect the shift to a direct combat role.

The Mark VII carries six medium lasers across the nose, wings, and aft positions, supplemented by two nose-mounted small lasers. A Fusion 200 engine provides safe thrust 4 and maximum thrust 6. Thirteen tons of standard armor protect the hull, with nose concentration. A 31-ton cargo bay is retained alongside the weapons systems. The Mark VII's VTOL hover capability allows it to land in rough terrain without prepared strips, an advantage over conventional aerodyne designs that require prepared surfaces. The design's reliance on short-range energy weapons makes it most effective in close engagements, and it performs poorly against opponents who can maintain standoff range.

The Mark VII-C substitutes Clan medium pulse lasers for IS medium lasers and fits Clan double heat sinks, improving thermal efficiency while retaining the same combat silhouette. Clan standard armor runs one ton lighter than the IS version but provides superior protection values.
text.deployment: The Mk.III Assault Craft was assigned to HAF aerospace wings tasked with direct fighter suppression during landing operations. Unlike the Mk.II, which operated as part of landing craft formations, the Mk.III could operate independently and served with WarShip and JumpShip flotillas as a close-escort asset. Its enhanced thrust allowed crews to pursue and engage enemy fighters rather than simply defend during descent, and HAF squadrons valued it as both a deterrent and an active interceptor. The design entered service in 2451 and remained the most capable combat craft in the Ares family through the late Age of War, keeping its front-line assignment well into the Star League era even after the introduction of the lighter successor frames.
text.battleHistory:
IncStar Dynamics introduced the Mk.III Assault Craft in 2451 as the third branch of the original Ares family, joining the Mk.I long-range landing craft and the Mk.II close attack landing craft on the same base hull. Where the Mk.I carried cargo and the Mk.II provided escort suppression, the Mk.III was built for direct fighter engagement. Its more powerful engine gave it the thrust to pursue and intercept, and reinforced armor allowed it to absorb damage that would have disabled the other marks. All three designs operated together in HAF landing wings through the Age of War and into the Star League period, each branch complementing the others on contested planetary approaches.

The fall of the Star League and the Succession Wars stripped away the manufacturing base that supported the original Ares family. IncStar Dynamics dissolved during the First Succession War, having already dropped the Ares name as the collapse of the Ares Conventions made the designation politically awkward. By 2824, a simplified but robust successor emerged: the Mark VII, the standard-technology heir to the Mk.I long-range landing craft branch. Produced at factories across the Successor States and the Taurian Concordat, the Mark VII carried the landing craft lineage forward while the close attack branch of the Mk.II was absorbed into broader doctrine and the assault craft branch of the Mk.III lay dormant.

The Mark VII-C emerged in 2841 with Clan technology. Clan Ghost Bear produced it at their Tseng Facility in orbit around Alshain, and Clan Jade Falcon added production at the Falcon's Roost Orbital Assembly Plant on Sudeten in 3074. Both the IS Mark VII and the Clan Mark VII-C share the introduction year of 2841 despite the decades of isolation between the two civilizations, leading historians to conclude that both designs evolved independently from a shared earlier ancestor rather than one copying the other.

The assault craft branch of the family did not stay dormant permanently. Universal Air maintained the original Ares design archives through the Succession Wars and the Clan Invasion era. After merging with Federated Boeing, the company restarted Ares attack craft production in 3066 and introduced the Mark IX in 3077, completing the revival of the third branch and reuniting all three lines of the original Ares family under active production for the first time since the Star League era.
text.notes: Modified from XTR: to be legal.

text.overview: The Ares Close Assault Landing Craft, designated the Mk.II, emerged just six years after the Mk.I as a purpose-built fire support variant of the Ares family. Developed by IncStar Dynamics, the Mk.II replaced a portion of the standard landing craft's cargo capacity with an additional battery of large lasers, transforming the design from a transport with self-defense weaponry into a genuine close-support gunship. Where the Mk.I was optimized for cargo delivery, the Mk.II was intended to serve as a heavy escort, clearing fighter screens and suppressing ground targets as the cargo-laden landing craft completed their runs. The design was fielded by the Hegemony Armed Forces alongside the Mk.I, operating in mixed squadrons that paired the Mk.II's fire support with the Mk.I's cargo capacity and the Mk.III's fighter-engagement role.
text.capabilities:
The Mk.II distinguishes itself from the Mk.I primarily in its offensive armament. Three large lasers supplement the existing weapons layout, dramatically increasing the craft's ability to engage enemy fighters and ground targets at extended range. This heavier weapons load demands more heat management, and the Mk.II carries additional heat sinks over the base design to handle the added thermal output. The reduced cargo capacity is a deliberate trade, reflecting the craft's shift from transport to fire support.

The primitive fusion engine and armor profile closely mirror those of the Mk.I, providing the same basic mobility and protection envelope. Forward and aft defense is retained through the same combination of nose and aft medium lasers that proved effective on the base landing craft, giving the Mk.II adequate self-protection even when operating away from formation cover. The aerodyne configuration is identical to the base design, keeping maintenance and training requirements consistent across the family. Like all Ares variants, the Mk.II carries the performance limitations common to primitive-era aerospace design, including reduced maneuverability compared to later standard-technology successors.
text.deployment: The Mk.II Close Assault Landing Craft was assigned in small numbers to HAF landing craft wings, typically one or two craft per squadron. Its role was strictly fire support: clearing fighter screens and providing heavy ground-attack capability as Mk.I craft completed their cargo deliveries. Mk.II crews developed aggressive approach profiles, closing quickly and engaging hostile fighters before breaking off to allow the cargo craft through. The design was not assigned independent transport duties, relying on the Mk.I for cargo work and the Mk.III for direct fighter engagement. Deployment alongside sister craft in mixed squadrons allowed each variant to focus on its designed mission, a combined-arms approach that defined HAF landing operations throughout the Age of War.
text.battleHistory:
The Hegemony Armed Forces recognized early that the Mk.I, however capable as a cargo carrier, could not simultaneously deliver heavy armor and provide the concentrated fire support needed to suppress determined fighter opposition. IncStar Dynamics' solution was to build the Mk.II Close Assault Landing Craft on the same base hull as the Mk.I, introducing it in 2444 alongside the Mk.III Assault Craft. The three designs formed a deliberate family: the Mk.I as the long-range landing craft branch, the Mk.II as the close attack landing craft branch, and the Mk.III as the dedicated fighter-engagement branch. Sharing a common hull simplified logistics, training, and maintenance across the three types.

The Mk.II served in mixed HAF landing wings through the Age of War and into the Star League period, operating alongside its two sister designs. Crews developed aggressive escort profiles, closing to maximum effective laser range before breaking off to allow Mk.I cargo craft through contested airspace. The type earned a reputation for sustained close-range fire, often remaining in hostile airspace longer than doctrine required to ensure the landing craft completed their drops.

When the redesigned Mk.IV successor frame arrived in 2476, the close assault escort role was gradually absorbed into the Mk.III Assault Craft lineage, which offered superior thrust and maneuverability for the fighter-engagement mission. The Mk.II transitioned to second-line duties and was eventually superseded entirely by the Mark VII following the Star League's collapse. The close attack landing craft branch itself did not produce a direct named successor the way the long-range landing craft branch produced the Mark VII, or the assault craft branch produced the Ares Mark IX. The Mk.II's escort role was instead folded into the broader capabilities of those surviving lines.
text.notes: Stat's adjusted from XTR: to be legal.

text.overview: The Ares Landing Craft was the Terran Hegemony's answer to the hazardous problem of orbit-to-surface transport under fire. Designed by IncStar Dynamics and introduced in 2438, the Ares replaced a generation of converted merchant vessels that either sacrificed cargo capacity for self-defense weapons or lacked the firepower to survive contested planetary approaches. The Hegemony Armed Forces commissioned the design around the time of the Ares Conventions, and the craft's name reflected that era's cooperative military spirit. A 65-ton cargo bay, a heavy weapons array, and primitive but robust armor made the Ares the definitive combat landing craft of its generation, providing HAF ground commanders reliable orbit-to-surface access under conditions that would have destroyed earlier designs. Its success prompted IncStar Dynamics to develop several specialized variants tailored to the diverse combat roles that emerged from early Age of War operations.
text.capabilities:
The Ares Mk.I carries an armament designed to punch through fighter screens before they can close. Two medium lasers in the nose give the craft forward bite, while a pair of LRM-15 launchers in the wings extend its reach to ranges where opposing fighters struggle to respond effectively. Two additional medium lasers in the aft position protect against pursuit. Sixteen heat sinks manage the thermal load from sustained fire. The primitive fusion engine delivers a safe thrust of 3 and maximum thrust of 5, adequate for atmospheric transit and planetary approaches but not suited to prolonged deep-space pursuit.

The cargo bay holds 65 tons behind two doors, large enough to accommodate the heavy tracked vehicles of the era. Twenty-four tons of primitive armor protect the hull, with heavier concentration at the nose to resist head-on fighter attacks during descent. The aerodyne configuration makes the craft dependent on prepared surfaces or low-speed hover approaches, a constraint later marks addressed more fully. Crew requirements consist of a single officer and four enlisted personnel, modest for a vessel of this firepower.
text.deployment: The Mk.I served as the primary orbit-to-surface transport of the Hegemony Armed Forces during the Age of War, assigned to deliver heavy armor and cargo to contested planetary surfaces. Typical mission profiles paired the Mk.I with Mk.II Close Assault craft, which suppressed enemy fighter cover while the standard landing craft completed their cargo runs. The 65-ton bay accommodated heavy tracked vehicles up to the largest battle tanks of the era. HAF commanders deployed the design in squadron formations, assigning individual craft to specific armored or mechanized units for the duration of ground campaigns. Its primitive technology and limited performance envelope restricted the Mk.I to conventional atmospheric operations, rarely encountered in deep-space or orbital roles beyond basic transit runs between DropShips and landing zones.
text.battleHistory:
Before the Ares entered service, the Hegemony Armed Forces relied on converted merchant craft that proved dangerously inadequate under contested conditions. These vessels either carried too little self-defense weaponry to deter aggressive fighter screens, or sacrificed cargo capacity for weapons that still fell short of purpose-built military standards. IncStar Dynamics' proposal, developed as the Ares Conventions were reshaping inter-state military agreements in the Inner Sphere, addressed both failings in a single purpose-built design.

Introduced in 2438, the Mk.I entered HAF service as the primary orbit-to-surface transport for armored and mechanized units and established the hull that would define the entire Ares lineage. IncStar Dynamics built the Mk.II Close Assault Landing Craft and the Mk.III Assault Craft on this same base frame, creating a three-branch family from one design. The Mk.I represented the long-range landing craft branch, the Mk.II became the close attack landing craft branch, and the Mk.III became the dedicated attack craft branch. All three entered service within thirteen years and operated together in mixed HAF landing wings through the Age of War and into the early Star League period.

A lighter successor frame arrived in 2476 with the Mk.IV, ten tons lighter and slightly more maneuverable while retaining the same cargo and armor values. The Mk.V and Mk.VI carried the same lineage forward. These successor marks were themselves eventually replaced after the Star League's collapse by the Mark VII, which carried the long-range landing craft branch into the Succession Wars era under standard Inner Sphere technology. IncStar Dynamics dissolved during the First Succession War, having already dropped the Ares name as the collapse of the Ares Conventions made the designation politically awkward in the fractured Inner Sphere.

production.manufacturer: Clyde Shipyards|Federated-Boeing Interstellar Ltd. (Formerly Universal Air)|Salvatore Inc.

text.deployment: The standard Arondight represents the original production configuration as designed by Federated-Boeing Interstellar. Entering service in 3075, it was the first purpose-built Pocket WarShip fielded by the Armed Forces of the Federated Suns, incorporating direct feedback from the Medusans mercenary unit and their operational experience with Pocket WarShip Excaliburs. The base configuration centers its offensive capability around capital-grade missile systems supplemented by extensive conventional weaponry, providing a balanced approach that gives the standard Arondight flexibility against both WarShip-class targets and conventional aerospace threats. This makes it the preferred configuration for general fleet escort duties within the AFFS naval arm.

production.manufacturer: Refit - Federated-Boeing Interstellar Ltd. (Formerly Universal Air)

text.capabilities: The Refit variant restores the nose-mounted Kraken-T tele-operated missile launcher alongside a single Heavy Sub-Capital Cannon, two Gauss rifles, four ER medium lasers, and three anti-missile systems in the nose arc. The broadside armament remains identical to the SCC variant, with four Light Sub-Capital Cannons, four Piranha launchers, four rotary AC/5s, five ER medium lasers, and five anti-missile systems per side. The aft arc retains the Screen Launcher, dual Gauss rifles, four ER medium lasers, and three anti-missile systems. By reducing the number of nose-mounted capital cannons, the Refit variant increases cargo capacity to approximately 568 tons while maintaining the same ferro-aluminum armor protection, two hundred double heat sinks, and two small craft bays found across all Arondight configurations.
text.deployment: The Refit variant entered service in 3082 as a post-Jihad configuration balancing the proven firepower of the Arondight platform with increased logistical flexibility. Its expanded cargo capacity made it better suited for extended patrol and escort operations during the Republic era, when the AFFS transitioned from wartime offensive operations to peacetime force projection and border security duties.

production.manufacturer: Clyde Shipyards|Federated-Boeing Interstellar Ltd. (Formerly Universal Air)|Refit - Federated-Boeing Emergency Refit Yard

text.deployment: The SCC variant entered service in 3077 and was deployed with AFFS naval task forces during the final campaigns of the Jihad. Its enhanced ballistic armament proved far more reliable against the layered anti-missile defenses employed by Word of Blake naval formations, and the variant quickly became the preferred configuration for direct engagement missions against enemy Pocket WarShips and escort vessels.

production.manufacturer: O'Neil Yards - Titan Yards

text.capabilities:
The Assault Triumph stands as a radical departure from the original transport-focused design, transforming the platform into a heavily armed combined-arms assault ship. At 8,000 tons, it carries a mixed force of six aerospace fighters, six BattleMeks, twenty-four heavy combat vehicles, and six battle armor squads alongside over 854 tons of cargo and supplies. This configuration enables it to deliver most of a combined-arms formation in a single drop.

The weapons fit is dramatically upgraded, with concentrated nose firepower built around multiple ER PPCs supported by LRM-20 racks for long-range engagement. Broadside batteries of ER large lasers and LB-X autocannons provide devastating coverage against both air and ground targets, while 135 double heat sinks ensure the vessel can sustain continuous fire from its entire weapons array without overheating. Armor protection nearly doubles compared to the standard model, with 820 points of coverage enabling the Assault Triumph to survive the contested landings that proved fatal to so many of its predecessors. This combination of transport capacity, firepower, and survivability makes it one of the most capable aerodyne assault ships in service.
text.deployment: The Assault Triumph was developed at the Titan Yards on Terra following the Word of Blake's capture of those facilities in 3062. Designed to support Blakist Level III combined-arms formations, the Assault Triumph saw extensive deployment during the Jihad, where its heavy armament and substantial armor enabled it to force contested landings that would have been suicidal for standard Triumphs. Blakist forces used the type across numerous theaters during the conflict, and its ability to deliver a mixed force of Meks, vehicles, fighters, and battle armor made it a cornerstone of Word of Blake assault operations. Following the Jihad, captured examples entered service with several Coalition member states.

text.capabilities: The Battle Armor configuration uses the Aurora's modular bay inserts to carry twenty-four squads of battle armor supported by eight light vehicles. The battle armor bays include room for additional supplies, giving this configuration approximately 148 tons of total cargo storage. The standard Aurora weapons fit applies: two Gauss rifles and two ER medium lasers in the nose, paired ER PPCs on each wing, and two Gauss rifles with two large pulse lasers covering the aft arc. Fifty double heat sinks manage the thermal load. A crew of 195 operates this configuration, reflecting the substantial personnel needed to support battle armor operations.
text.deployment: The standard Aurora configuration represents the baseline troop transport variant as originally designed by Dynamico Limited and Shipil Company. Entering service in 3062, this configuration maximizes the type's signature modular bay system to carry a combined-arms force of BattleMechs and infantry, providing commanders with a versatile transport capable of delivering a balanced ground force in a single landing. The standard configuration proved itself during the FedCom Civil War, where its ability to rapidly deploy mixed formations gave loyalist forces critical flexibility during the fast-moving campaign on Kentares IV and New Avalon. It remains the most widely produced Aurora variant, with examples serving in nearly every major Inner Sphere military.

text.capabilities: The Cargo configuration maximizes the Aurora's hauling capacity by fitting all four modular bays for freight storage, achieving approximately 740 tons of total cargo capacity. This transforms the military transport into an armored merchant vessel capable of operating in hostile space lanes. The standard weapons fit remains unchanged, with two Gauss rifles and two ER medium lasers forward, paired ER PPCs on each broadside, and two Gauss rifles with two large pulse lasers aft. Fifty double heat sinks provide adequate thermal management. A crew of just eleven operates this configuration, the smallest complement of any Aurora variant.
text.deployment: The Cargo variant operates extensively along contested trade routes where its substantial weapons array provides protection that unarmed freighters cannot match. Many small mercenary commands have adopted this configuration as their primary transport, valuing the combination of cargo capacity and combat capability that the Aurora provides.

text.capabilities: The Combined Arms configuration carries ten light vehicles and positions for approximately forty-eight tons of conventional infantry, with 190 tons of cargo storage for supplies and equipment. This variant is designed for rapid deployment of integrated ground forces. The standard Aurora armament applies across all arcs: nose-mounted Gauss rifles and ER medium lasers, wing-mounted ER PPCs, and aft Gauss rifles with large pulse lasers. Fifty double heat sinks manage thermal output. A crew of 341 reflects the large number of embarked troops and their support personnel.
text.deployment: The Combined Arms configuration has proven popular with garrison and planetary defense forces that need to deploy integrated ground formations quickly. The ability to land a mixed force of vehicles and infantry from a single vessel simplifies operational planning and has made this variant a common sight in regional defense flotillas.

text.capabilities: The Carrier Vessel configuration replaces the standard modular bay inserts with facilities for four aerospace fighters alongside 140 tons of cargo capacity. This makes the Aurora CV a compact fighter carrier, capable of delivering a flight of aerospace assets to contested areas while retaining logistical flexibility. The weapons fit remains identical to the standard configuration: nose-mounted Gauss rifles and ER medium lasers, wing-mounted ER PPCs, and aft Gauss rifles with large pulse lasers. Fifty double heat sinks and a minimal crew of nineteen keep the vessel efficient and easy to operate.
text.deployment: The Carrier Vessel variant serves as a compact fighter transport for units that require aerospace support but lack the tonnage allocation for a dedicated carrier. Militia commands and small mercenary outfits have found the Aurora CV particularly attractive, as it provides both fighter transport and cargo capacity in a single affordable hull.

text.capabilities: The Gunship configuration dramatically increases the Aurora's combat capability. While retaining two aerospace fighter bays and 188 tons of cargo, the standard weaponry is substantially upgraded. The nose retains its twin Gauss rifles and ER medium lasers, but each wing mounts four ER PPCs, two heavy Gauss rifles, three Artemis IV-enhanced LRM-20 racks, and an anti-missile system. The aft arc retains its Gauss rifles and large pulse lasers. One hundred double heat sinks manage the tremendous thermal output of this weapons array, double the standard configuration's capacity. A crew of twenty-one operates this heavily armed variant, which serves as a dedicated fire support platform.
text.deployment: The Gunship variant serves as a dedicated fire support platform, typically operating alongside standard Aurora transports to provide covering fire during planetary assault and extraction operations. Its heavy weapons load makes it a formidable opponent for enemy DropShips and aerospace fighters, though its limited cargo capacity restricts independent operations.

text.capabilities: The Tanker configuration fills four of the Aurora's five bays with liquid storage modules, providing approximately 546 tons of liquid storage capacity alongside 140 tons of standard cargo in the fifth bay. This variant supports extended operations by providing fuel and fluid resupply to military formations in the field. The standard weapons fit is retained across all arcs: nose Gauss rifles and ER medium lasers, wing ER PPCs, and aft Gauss rifles with large pulse lasers. Fifty double heat sinks and a crew of eleven keep the Tanker operationally efficient.
text.deployment: The Tanker variant supports extended military operations by providing mobile fuel and fluid resupply capability. These vessels typically operate as part of larger task forces, extending the operational range of combat formations that would otherwise be limited by fuel constraints. The armed tanker concept has proven particularly valuable along the Periphery frontier.

text.capabilities: The Vehicle configuration carries twelve light vehicles across four modular bays, with 140 tons of cargo in the fifth bay. This provides transportation for a full company of light armor, making it ideal for rapid armored deployments. Each of four bays carries three vehicles, with the fifth reserved for supplies and spare parts. The standard Aurora weapons array covers all arcs: twin Gauss rifles and ER medium lasers forward, paired ER PPCs on each wing, and twin Gauss rifles with large pulse lasers aft. Fifty double heat sinks manage the thermal load, and a crew of seventy-one supports the embarked vehicle crews.
text.deployment: The Vehicle configuration transports armor companies for rapid deployment operations, serving as the primary light armored vehicle carrier for formations that do not require the heavier lift capacity of larger DropShips. This variant is commonly paired with BattleMech-carrying Auroras to deliver combined-arms battalions in a coordinated assault.

text.capabilities:
The Avenger mounts an impressive weapons array for its size, with firepower distributed across all firing arcs. The nose concentrates an AC/20, two AC/5s, an LRM-20 rack, two large lasers, and two medium lasers, while each wing carries a PPC, two AC/5s, an LRM-20, and two medium lasers. The aft arc mounts an AC/2, an LRM-20, and two medium lasers. Seventy single heat sinks manage the thermal load from this considerable arsenal. A small crew of fifteen operates the vessel alongside four dedicated gunners, keeping the Avenger's personnel requirements remarkably low for a combat vessel of its capability.

Uniquely among aerodyne craft designed for planetary operations, the Avenger features only a single rear maneuvering drive with no secondary transit drive. This requires an exotic interior layout where the orientation of up changes between atmospheric flight and space operations. In atmosphere, up points toward the vertical stabilizer; under thrust in space, up points toward the nose. The crew must reconfigure each room and its furniture between orientations, a process that takes approximately twenty minutes. Long corridors on the ground become lift shafts in space, with wall-mounted ladders providing access. The vessel also carries a small cargo bay and can perform strafing and bombing runs in support of ground forces.
text.deployment: The original Avenger entered service in 2816 and was adopted by every Successor State navy for planetary assault operations. These vessels were typically reserved for the largest engagements, forming the vanguard of attack formations alongside other assault craft. The Federated Suns maintained the most robust Avenger fleet throughout the Succession Wars thanks to Dynamico's production capacity at Delavan, while the Taurian Concordat stationed Avengers at contested jump points such as the Brinton system to deter Capellan and Canopian incursions. Despite the design's scarcity, its combination of firepower and agility made it a decisive asset in orbital combat across every major conflict of the era.

text.capabilities:
The (3048) variant replaced the original's seventy single heat sinks with double-strength models, dramatically improving sustained firepower management. Each pair of AC/5 autocannons in the nose and wings was replaced with a Poland Model A Gauss rifle, providing increased range and firepower without generating additional heat. ExoStar ER large lasers supplemented the original nose-mounted large lasers, while all eight medium lasers were replaced with Martell medium pulse lasers for improved close-range accuracy.

Each LRM-20 rack received an Artemis IV fire control system for enhanced missile tracking against maneuvering targets. ER PPCs replaced the standard models on each wing, extending engagement range significantly. The aft arc received an ER large laser in place of the AC/2, improving rear defense. These upgrades substantially increased the vessel's combat effectiveness at all ranges while maintaining the same armor protection and structural integrity as the original. The GM 9800i drive system and unique dual-orientation interior layout remained unchanged from the base design.
text.deployment: The upgraded Avenger entered production at Dynamico's Delavan facility in 3048, with joint production at Defiance Industries on Hesperus II following from 3055. These vessels were rapidly adopted across the Federated Commonwealth's naval forces, assuming the vanguard assault role from their predecessors. The upgraded variant proved particularly effective against Clan-grade opposition in the post-Invasion era, and its proven combat record led to expanded adoption. The Avenger's compact size and low crew requirements continued to make it an attractive assault platform for both state navies and well-funded mercenary commands.

text.overview: The NL-42 Battle Taxi is a two-hundred-ton boarding transport small craft originally designed by Blackwell Corporation on New Valencia. Introduced in 3053 as the military equivalent of the ubiquitous S-7A shuttle bus, the Battle Taxi was purpose-built for ship-to-ship boarding operations against DropShips, JumpShips, and WarShips. Its combination of speed, heavy armor protection, and generous troop capacity made it an immediate success with naval forces across the Inner Sphere, and the design was quickly licensed to manufacturers in every major Successor State. The craft's straightforward construction and reliable performance earned it a reputation as the standard small craft for marine assault operations, a role it continues to fill decades after its introduction.
text.capabilities:
The Battle Taxi relies on a safe thrust of three gravities, with a maximum acceleration of four and a half gravities, to close rapidly with target vessels during boarding actions. A pair of magnetic grapples and a hull-mounted tug adapter allow the craft to latch onto enemy DropShips, JumpShips, or even WarShips, pulling itself alongside to disgorge its marine contingent. If the tug adapter cannot achieve a proper seal, embarked marines can use magnetic boots and cutting tools to create alternate access points along the target hull.

Armament consists of paired extended-range large lasers mounted in the wing sections for long-range suppressive fire during approach, supplemented by four medium pulse lasers split between the wings for close-range defense. Thirty-two tons of standard armor provide substantial protection during the vulnerable approach phase. The craft's cargo hold accommodates fifty tons of personnel and equipment, typically two points of battle armor or three full platoons of conventional infantry. A crew of three operates the vessel, though a single pilot can manage the craft at reduced effectiveness if necessary.
text.deployment: The base NL-42 represents the standard production model as manufactured by Blackwell Corporation and its numerous licensees. This configuration has remained essentially unchanged since its introduction, reflecting the proven nature of the design's balance of approach speed, defensive firepower, and troop capacity for conventional ship-to-ship boarding missions across both naval and anti-piracy operations.
text.battleHistory:
The NL-42 emerged from Blackwell Corporation's extensive experience supporting Wolf's Dragoons, who had long relied on boarding operations as part of their combined-arms doctrine. The design drew on Star League-era boarding craft concepts, updated with technologies available in the early 3050s. Blackwell's close relationship with the Dragoons meant the craft was field-tested extensively before being offered on the open market, and the Dragoons' own variant, known as the Lupus, became the first operational model.

The design's immediate popularity led to rapid licensing across the Inner Sphere. Andurien AeroTech on Westover, Earthwerks Limited on Ares, Shipil Company on Skye, and Tomori Trans Industrial on Chatham all secured production rights, ensuring that every major Successor State gained access to the craft within a decade of its introduction. This broad manufacturing base reflected growing demand for dedicated boarding craft as naval operations expanded during the Clan Invasion era and the subsequent Civil War period.

The use of extended-range and pulse laser technology in the base design created a historical curiosity. Sarna records suggest the NL-42 class saw service during earlier, lower-technology eras of the Succession Wars, when such advanced weapon systems were unavailable. What weapons the earlier models carried remains undocumented, though the Lupus variant used by Wolf's Dragoons is confirmed to have mounted the full advanced weapons suite. The Jihad disrupted several production lines, especially Blackwell's facility on New Valencia, but the distributed manufacturing network ensured the Battle Taxi remained available throughout the conflict and into the post-Jihad era. Production continues at multiple sites across the Inner Sphere, with ownership changes reflecting the political upheavals of the Dark Age and ilClan periods.
