text.capabilities:
The original Fury is powered by a Hyperdyne 211 drive system providing a safe thrust of 1.5 gravities with a maximum of 2.5 gravities, adequate for a troop transport but unremarkable by military standards. Twenty-nine tons of standard armor provide modest protection across all arcs, though the coverage is thin compared to dedicated assault vessels. The weapons array reflects the Fury's role as a transport rather than a combatant, mounting a PPC, a pair of LRM-15 launchers, four large lasers, eight medium lasers, and four small lasers distributed across the nose, wings, and aft arcs. Seventy-eight single heat sinks manage the thermal load from this predominantly energy-based arsenal.

The interior accommodates four infantry platoons in dedicated bunkrooms, each equipped with three-tier bunks, storage lockers, and washroom facilities. The troops share a moderately sized mess area but have only a single small recreation space that must be used in shifts. Crew quarters are similarly cramped but feature larger personal storage lockers and reading lights. Eight light vehicle bays occupy the main cargo hold, accessed through the vessel's nose via a steep ramp that significantly impedes deployment speed. An additional 505 tons of general cargo capacity supports extended operations.
text.deployment: The original Fury served with every major Star League-era military and remained in widespread use throughout the Succession Wars. Its primary role was delivering infantry and light vehicles in the second wave of planetary assaults, operating behind better-armed DropShips like the Gazelle and under the protective umbrella of Leopard CV fighter carriers. Fury groups of three vessels became a standard formation, coordinating their limited defensive fire to improve survivability against enemy interceptors. The design saw service with virtually every Successor State and numerous mercenary commands, its simplicity and low operating costs ensuring its continued utility even as larger, more capable transports became increasingly scarce.

production.manufacturer: Brigadier Corporation|Diamond Garter Shipyards (a Division of Alliance Aerospace Group)

text.capabilities:
The redesigned (3056) variant retains the Hyperdyne 211 drive system and the same basic hull configuration but incorporates significant weapons modernization using recovered Star League technology. The standard PPC has been replaced with an extended-range model, and both LRM-15 launchers now feature Artemis IV fire control systems for improved missile accuracy. The small lasers have been removed entirely, replaced by two additional medium lasers that provide better damage output at more useful engagement ranges. Seventy-six single heat sinks manage the slightly increased thermal demands of the upgraded weapons suite.

The most significant non-weapons improvement is a factory-installed steel-cable winch system integrated into the cargo bay, capable of lifting vehicles weighing up to fifty tons. This directly addresses the steep cargo ramp that has been the Fury's most persistent design flaw, dramatically reducing vehicle loading and unloading times. The infantry accommodations and vehicle bay layout remain largely unchanged, still carrying four platoons and eight light vehicles with 504.5 tons of cargo capacity. The overall improvement in firepower and operational efficiency, while modest, substantially increases the Fury's survivability during contested landings.
text.deployment: The upgraded Fury was produced by the Brigadier Corporation on Gibson and initially distributed to Free Worlds League units stationed along the volatile Marik-Davion border. Several of the first production run were assigned to the Third Free Worlds League Guards on Zion, where rising tensions made combat deployment likely in the near term. The Free Worlds League Military was the primary recipient of the new production model, though export sales to other Successor States were anticipated. Despite the weapons improvements, tactical doctrine continued to emphasize combined operations with heavier escort vessels rather than independent deployment.

production.manufacturer: Boeing Interstellar|Deller, Bingham, and Fouts|Federated-Boeing Interstellar - Port Simon Shipyards

text.capabilities:
The original Gazelle is powered by a Star League V95 drive system providing a safe thrust of 1.5 gravities with a maximum of 2.5 gravities, consistent with its role as a transport rather than a combat vessel. Twenty-nine tons of standard armor provide basic protection, though the coverage is thin for a military vessel of its tonnage. The weapons array is limited, mounting a pair of PPCs, a large laser, a pair of LRM-15 launchers, four medium lasers, and four small lasers distributed across the nose, wings, and aft arcs. Seventy single heat sinks manage the thermal output of the predominantly energy-based weapons suite.

The interior is configured around a large vehicle bay capable of carrying fifteen light combat vehicles, accessed through the craft's nose ramp. Vehicle crews are accommodated in three bays on the second deck, each with facilities for one lance including four triple bunks and additional berths for support personnel. The DropShip crew occupies a bunkroom of similar size and fittings. With 818.5 tons of cargo capacity, the original model offers considerably greater endurance than later variants, a benefit of the lighter vehicles it was designed to carry.
text.deployment: The original Gazelle served throughout the Star League era as the standard light vehicle transport for combined-arms assault formations, operating alongside Fury infantry carriers and Leopard fighter escorts. Its generous cargo capacity made it well-suited to extended deployments in the Periphery during the Reunification War, where supply lines were often stretched thin. As heavier vehicles entered service, the original configuration was progressively replaced by the modified heavy vehicle variant, and surviving unmodified Gazelles were either converted or relegated to rear-area logistical roles.

production.manufacturer: Deller, Bingham, and Fouts|Yare Industries Inc. - Yare Shipyards

text.capabilities:
The upgraded (3055) variant is a comprehensive modernization weighing 3,400 tons, an increase of five hundred tons over the original. The vehicle capacity is split between twelve heavy vehicle bays in the nose and three light vehicle bays further aft, significantly reducing the deployment bottleneck that plagued earlier models. Three hundred forty-seven tons of cargo capacity restores much of the operational endurance lost in the heavy vehicle conversion.

The weapons array received targeted upgrades using recovered Star League technology. Standard PPCs and large lasers were replaced with extended-range variants, including the Defiance 1001 ER PPC, while the LRM batteries received Artemis IV fire control systems for improved missile accuracy. Standard medium lasers were upgraded to pulse models for enhanced close-range accuracy. Forty-five double heat sinks replaced the original seventy singles, providing superior thermal management with reduced mass. Armor protection was slightly increased to 504 points. The overall effect is a markedly more capable vessel that addresses the most critical shortcomings of the Succession Wars-era configuration.
text.deployment: Produced by New Syrtis Shipyards beginning in 3055, the upgraded Gazelle was adopted primarily by the Armed Forces of the Federated Commonwealth, which became the major buyer of the new variant. Several upgraded Gazelles saw their first combat deployment during operations to suppress unrest in the Skye March, where initial reports confirmed that the modernized weapons array significantly improved the vessel's defensive capability. The split vehicle bay configuration proved particularly valuable in fast-paced operations where rapid deployment was critical, reducing ground vulnerability compared to the older single-bay design.

production.manufacturer: Deller, Bingham, and Fouts|Federated-Boeing Interstellar - Port Simon Shipyards

text.capabilities:
The Succession Wars-era heavy vehicle modification represents the most widely fielded configuration of the Gazelle. The nose vehicle bay was enlarged to accommodate fifteen heavy combat vehicles, including main battle tanks weighing up to one hundred tons. This expansion required significant internal restructuring, reducing crew quarters to their most cramped configuration and slashing cargo capacity to just 68.5 tons. The resulting conditions make the heavy vehicle Gazelle one of the most uncomfortable DropShips in regular military service.

The sixty-meter by eighteen-meter vehicle bay is accessed through a single nose ramp, creating a severe deployment bottleneck. Unloading fifteen heavy tanks through this single point of egress takes considerably longer than comparable multi-ramp designs, leaving the vessel vulnerable on the ground during deployment operations. The weapons array and drive system remain identical to the original model, with seventy single heat sinks and the same Star League V95 drive providing unchanged performance. The limited cargo capacity means that this variant must operate from established forward bases or receive frequent resupply.
text.deployment: The heavy vehicle Gazelle became the standard configuration by the mid-Succession Wars era, fielded by every Successor State and most major mercenary commands. Experienced commanders learned to minimize ground time by conducting pre-planned rapid deployment sequences, though even veteran crews found the single-ramp design frustratingly slow. The vessel typically deployed in combined formations with Fury infantry carriers and Leopard CVs providing fighter cover. Many Gazelles destroyed during the Succession Wars were lost not in space but on the ground while unloading, particularly when embarking inexperienced vehicle units unfamiliar with the tight bay configuration.

production.manufacturer: Andurien AeroTech

text.overview: The Gorgon is a carrier DropShip developed in the early thirty-second century to provide dedicated aerospace fighter transport and deployment capability. Designed to fill the gap left by the loss of WarShip-based carrier capacity during the Jihad, the Gorgon offers a practical solution for military forces that need to project aerospace power without the expense of maintaining true capital ships. The design prioritizes fighter bay capacity and rapid launch operations over direct combat capability, relying on its embarked fighter wings and escort vessels for protection. The Gorgon has found buyers among several Inner Sphere militaries seeking affordable carrier capability.
text.capabilities: The Gorgon is a military DropShip optimized for aerospace fighter transport and deployment operations. Its internal layout is dominated by fighter bays and their associated maintenance, arming, and launch facilities, giving the vessel the ability to embark, maintain, and rapidly deploy a substantial fighter complement. Defensive armament is secondary to the carrier mission, with weapons systems positioned primarily to provide point defense against incoming missiles and fighters that penetrate the escort screen. Armor protection is adequate to survive glancing hits and fighter strafing runs but insufficient to sustain direct engagement with assault DropShips or Pocket WarShips. The drive system provides sufficient acceleration to maintain formation with fleet elements while allowing the Gorgon to position itself behind the combat line where its fighters can launch without exposing the carrier to direct fire. The vessel's combat contribution is measured primarily through its embarked fighters rather than its own weapons systems, making the Gorgon's effectiveness directly proportional to the quality and quantity of its aerospace complement. Support facilities aboard allow extended operations without returning to a base for fighter maintenance.
text.deployment: The standard Gorgon Carrier serves in its baseline aerospace fighter carrier configuration, providing fighter transport and deployment capability to naval task forces. These vessels typically operate in the second line of fleet formations, relying on escort vessels and their own fighter wings for protection while serving as mobile bases for sustained aerospace operations.
text.battleHistory:
The Gorgon emerged from the post-Jihad recognition that affordable carrier capability was essential for any military force seeking to project power across interstellar distances. The destruction of numerous WarShips during the Jihad had left most Inner Sphere navies without dedicated carrier assets, forcing them to rely on multi-role DropShips with limited fighter capacity to provide aerospace support for planetary operations.

The Gorgon was designed to address this gap with a purpose-built carrier that could be produced at conventional DropShip facilities rather than requiring the specialized infrastructure of a WarShip yard. By focusing exclusively on the carrier mission and accepting limitations in direct combat capability, the designers created a vessel that could be produced more quickly and cheaply than any previous dedicated carrier design.

Initial production deliveries went to forces that had suffered the most severe carrier losses during the Jihad, with the design quickly proving its worth in exercises and limited combat deployments. The Gorgon's ability to sustain fighter operations for extended periods without returning to base gave fleet commanders a capability they had lacked since the loss of their WarShip carriers. The class has since entered service with several Inner Sphere militaries, establishing itself as a practical and cost-effective solution to the post-Jihad carrier shortage.

production.manufacturer: Kintetsu Stellar Systems

text.overview:
The Hoshiryokou is a small 800-ton civilian Aerodyne DropShip originating from the early years of the Draconis Combine. First produced in 2480, the vessel was originally designed as a combined cargo and passenger carrier for commercial interstellar operations. However, the design aged badly in its original role, struggling to compete with newer and more capable merchant vessels.

Facing obsolescence, the Hoshiryokou was redesigned by Kintetsu Stellar Systems to serve as a space tug, a role that proved far more successful than its original merchant configuration. In this new capacity, the vessel became a popular utility craft operating in and around space stations, orbital complexes, and merchant fleet staging areas throughout the Draconis Combine.
text.capabilities:
The Hoshiryokou tug variant is built around its naval tug adaptor, which allows the vessel to dock with and maneuver cargo containers, disabled spacecraft, and orbital structures. The hull mounts ten external cargo container hardpoints, each rated for ten tons, providing flexible cargo-hauling capability without requiring internal bay space. This external configuration allows rapid loading and unloading at orbital facilities.

Defensive armament is minimal, consisting of a nose-mounted large laser and two small lasers, with a single small laser covering the aft arc. Eight single heat sinks manage the modest thermal load. The vessel's 388 points of armor provide surprisingly robust protection for a civilian craft of its size, reflecting the hazardous working conditions of orbital tug operations where collisions and debris impacts are constant risks. A crew of fifteen operates the vessel, with safe thrust of 5g providing excellent maneuverability for precision docking and towing work. Internal cargo space is limited to seven tons, as the tug relies primarily on its external container system for hauling capacity.
text.deployment: The standard Hoshiryokou represents the original cargo and passenger configuration as first produced by Kintetsu Stellar Systems. Designed in the early years of the Draconis Combine, this small 800-ton aerodyne was initially intended to serve the growing merchant trade between Combine worlds, carrying modest cargo loads and a handful of passengers aboard its compact hull. While the design would later be redesigned as a space tug, the original transport variant saw widespread use among independent traders and small shipping concerns operating within Combine space, valued for its low operating costs and ability to dock with smaller JumpShip collars.
text.battleHistory:
The Hoshiryokou entered service in 2480 during the early expansion of the Draconis Combine, originally serving as a small cargo and passenger vessel on commercial routes within Combine space. While adequate for the era, the design struggled to remain competitive as newer merchant DropShips with greater capacity and better amenities entered the market. By the mid-twenty-sixth century, the Hoshiryokou's commercial viability had declined significantly.

Kintetsu Stellar Systems, facing near-bankruptcy, redesigned the Hoshiryokou for the space tug role as a last attempt to find a viable market for the aging hull. This conversion proved to be a masterstroke of engineering pragmatism. The tug variant found immediate demand among space station operators, orbital facility managers, and merchant fleet logisticians who needed a reliable utility vessel for in-system hauling, cargo container shuttling, and general orbital operations. The Hoshiryokou's compact size and robust construction, liabilities in the competitive merchant market, became assets in the tug role where maneuverability and durability mattered more than passenger comfort or cargo volume.

production.manufacturer: Boeing Interstellar

text.overview:
The Interdictor class Pocket WarShip is a 9,400-ton Aerodyne assault vessel developed by the Word of Blake Protectorate in 3074. Designed after the Blakists suffered significant WarShip losses, the Interdictor was engineered to fill the gap using newly available sub-capital weapon technologies mounted on a DropShip-scale hull. The design uses the Achilles class assault DropShip as its structural basis, adapted to carry weapons capable of threatening true WarShip targets.

Built for speed and overwhelming firepower, the Interdictor was conceived as an interceptor capable of running down and engaging inbound or outbound vessels. Its combination of sub-capital grade armament, heavy armor protection, and exceptional thrust performance makes it one of the most dangerous DropShip-class combatants ever fielded, capable of engaging targets far above its weight class.
text.capabilities:
The Republic of the Sphere's SCC variant removes the capital and sub-capital missile launchers in favor of two nose-mounted medium sub-capital cannons and a sub-capital laser in each wing. The nose is further reinforced with three heavy PPCs, three MML-9 racks with Artemis IV guidance, and three large variable-speed pulse lasers. Each broadside mounts a sub-capital laser, four heavy PPCs, seven large variable-speed pulse lasers, two ER PPCs, three MML-9 racks with Artemis IV, and three anti-missile systems.

The aft arc carries two heavy PPCs, three large variable-speed pulse lasers, three Artemis-guided MML-9 racks, and an anti-missile system. Two hundred forty-four double heat sinks handle the thermal load. Two small craft bays and 509 tons of cargo are carried. The 2,053 points of heavy ferro-aluminum armor and safe thrust of seven are retained from the original design. A crew of eighty-six operates the vessel.
text.deployment: The SCC variant became the standard Interdictor configuration for the Republic of the Sphere's naval forces from 3078 onward. Republic commanders deployed these vessels extensively as system patrol craft and rapid-response interceptors, leveraging their speed and heavy armament to dominate contested space lanes during the post-Jihad reconstruction period and into the early Dark Age.
text.battleHistory:
The Interdictor emerged from the Word of Blake's urgent need to replace WarShip losses sustained during the Jihad. Blakist engineers adapted the proven Achilles assault DropShip hull to mount sub-capital weapons, creating a vessel that could threaten WarShip-class targets at a fraction of the cost and construction time. The original 3074 design was optimized for vessel interdiction and capture, carrying marine complements and boarding equipment alongside its heavy armament. An anti-shipping variant followed in 3075, trading marine capacity for capital-grade missile launchers.

Following the defeat of the Word of Blake, the Republic of the Sphere acquired Interdictor production capability and developed its own variant in 3078. Republic engineers refined the weapons loadout based on combat experience during the Jihad, emphasizing sub-capital cannons and expanded missile systems over capital launchers. The Republic continued to develop the design, introducing a further refined variant in 3115 that incorporated networking systems to enhance coordination with allied vessels. The Interdictor remained a key element of Republic naval doctrine throughout the Dark Age.

production.manufacturer: Andurien AeroTech (A Division of Free Worlds Defense Industries)|BBP Industries|Tharkad Aerospace Group

text.capabilities:
The Intruder distributes heavy weaponry evenly across its hull, making the vessel dangerous from any angle. The nose mounts a PPC, an LRM-20, an AC/5, and two medium lasers. Each broadside carries extensive firepower across two weapon bays: the forward arc mounts a PPC, an LRM-20, a large laser, and two medium lasers, while the rear arc adds two PPCs, an AC/10, an AC/5, two SRM-6 racks, and four medium lasers. The aft is defended by an LRM-20, two large lasers, and two medium lasers. One hundred thirteen single heat sinks manage the thermal load.

The vessel carries a company of marines for boarding and ground operations, housed alongside three large training bays that double as recreational spaces. Medical facilities include an operating theater with two tables, a six-bed intensive care unit, and a dispensary. The command center features mapboards, tactical intelligence displays, and battle computers rivaling those of command Union and Overlord variants. Two small craft bays carry fighters or shuttles, and the 844-ton cargo bay can be modified to transport light vehicles. The Intruder's unique landing gear retracts upward into the hull rather than outward, leaving the hull flush with the ground and nearly impossible to sabotage from below.
text.deployment: The original Intruder has served with military forces across the Inner Sphere since 2655, valued for its independent operational capability and versatile mission profile. The Free Worlds League fielded the largest numbers thanks to Andurien AeroTech's production, while BBP Industries and Tharkad Aerospace Group supplied the design to additional states. A notable Capellan Confederation variant introduced in 2905 modified the rear-arc autocannons for heavier firepower at the cost of fuel capacity.

production.manufacturer: Andurien AeroTech (A Division of Free Worlds Defense Industries)|Tharkad Aerospace Group

text.capabilities:
The 3056 upgrade replaces the entire weapons array with advanced technology equivalents. PPCs become ER PPCs throughout, while the nose AC/5 is replaced with an Ultra AC/5 and the broadside autocannons give way to Gauss rifles. All LRM-20 and SRM-6 racks receive Artemis IV fire control systems for improved accuracy. Standard large lasers are replaced with a mix of large pulse lasers and ER large lasers, and all sixteen medium lasers become medium pulse lasers. The switch to one hundred double heat sinks from the original's one hundred thirteen single sinks dramatically improves sustained-fire capability.

Infantry capacity drops from four platoons to three, but the additional cargo space of 850 tons slightly exceeds the original's 844. The crew complement decreases from 159 to 130 through improved automation. Fighter bays, medical facilities, command center, and the distinctive hull-flush landing system remain unchanged from the original design.
text.deployment: The upgraded Intruder entered production at Andurien AeroTech in 3056 and has seen service primarily with the Free Worlds League and its successor states. The advanced weapons and electronics package made these vessels particularly effective in the post-Clan Invasion threat environment, and the design has remained in active service through the Dark Age era.

production.manufacturer: Dell Aerospace Industriplex|WC Aerospace Annex

text.overview: The Isegrim is an assault DropShip born from a secret collaboration between Clan Wolf and Clan Wolf-in-Exile during the Jihad. Scientists and technicians from both Clans, brought together by circumstance when Wolf vessels sought repairs at the Exile yards on Arc-Royal, covertly developed the design to counter the Word of Blake's Interdictor Pocket WarShip. Based on a modified Noruff hull, the Isegrim first launched from the WC Aerospace Annex on Arc-Royal in 3083. The design has since proliferated through both Wolf factions and their trading partners, becoming one of the more widely distributed Clan assault DropShips of the post-Jihad era.
text.capabilities: The Isegrim is an 8,500-ton military aerodyne assault DropShip designed specifically to outperform the Blakist Interdictor. Its drive system provides acceleration superior to its intended opponent, allowing the Isegrim to dictate engagement range and pursue or disengage at will. Ninety-four and a half tons of Ferro-Aluminum armor concentrated on the nose and sides provides excellent protection against frontal attacks, though the aft arc remains the vessel's most vulnerable aspect. The weapons suite combines sub-capital missiles with a devastating conventional battery of HAG 40 autocannons, ER PPCs, Large Pulse Lasers, and ATM 12 launchers, giving the Isegrim overwhelming firepower against targets up to and including Pocket WarShips. Twelve anti-missile systems provide comprehensive point defense coverage. The vessel also carries Elemental marine squads for boarding operations, and its bays can accommodate Piranha and Manta Ray sub-capital missile reloads. The combination of speed, protection, and firepower makes the Isegrim a formidable opponent in any naval engagement, though its relatively small size limits its ability to absorb sustained fire from capital-class weapons.
text.deployment: The standard Isegrim serves in its baseline assault configuration, providing anti-ship and escort capability for Clan Wolf and Clan Wolf-in-Exile naval formations. These vessels typically operate in pairs or small Stars, using their superior speed to run down enemy vessels or screen larger fleet assets from Pocket WarShip threats.
text.battleHistory:
The Isegrim's origins lie in the desperate circumstances of the Jihad, when Word of Blake space forces dealt severe blows to both Clan Wolf and Clan Wolf-in-Exile. When Wolf vessels were forced to use the Exile naval yards on Arc-Royal for repairs, scientists and technicians from both factions began collaborating without authorization on a design to counter the Blakist Interdictor. The resulting vessel, built on a proven Noruff hull, was engineered to outrun, outgun, and outlast the enemy that had been decimating Wolf shipping.

Both Clans began production separately, with the Exiles launching their first Isegrim from Arc-Royal in 3083 to considerable fanfare from the Lyran Alliance. The celebration turned to alarm within the year when Clan Wolf Isegrims appeared in orbit above Tamar, revealing that the main-line Wolves had established their own production facility on Dell. Archon demanded answers, and Khan Phelan Kell launched an investigation that included the execution of three Exile scientists, though the deliberate pace of the inquiry suggested political theater rather than genuine outrage.

Despite the controversy, the Isegrim proliferated rapidly. Within two years, the class was seen in large numbers throughout both Lyran space and the Wolf Occupation Zone. Clan Wolf proved willing to trade the design for scarce commodities, selling an entire year's production run to Clan Diamond Shark in exchange for HarJel supplies. Clan Hell's Horses and Clan Nova Cat also expressed interest, and the Exiled Wolves accommodated buyers as well. The Isegrim has since become one of the most widely distributed Clan assault DropShip designs of the post-Jihad era.

production.manufacturer: Krester Ship Construction|Krester Ship Construction|Krester Ship Construction|Majesty Metals and Manufacturing|Markesan Aeronautics|Matabushi Inc.|Nimakachi Fusion Products Ltd.|Rashpur-Owens Inc.|Rockwell-Vasquez Starcraft Inc.|Shipil Company|Taurus Orbital Engineering Corporation

text.overview: The Jumbo is one of the oldest DropShip designs still recognized in modern naval records, with origins predating the formal DropShip concept itself. Emerging during the early years of interstellar colonization, the Jumbo began as a generic classification for large sub-light cargo vessels before eventually solidifying into a specific 14,800-ton design. At its peak, the Jumbo was the premier bulk cargo carrier serving the expanding colonies of the Terran Alliance and its successor states. Though long since supplanted by the more efficient Mule class and other modern transports, the Jumbo's influence on cargo DropShip design remains significant, and a handful of these ancient vessels continued operating well into the thirty-first century.
text.capabilities: The Jumbo is a massive 14,800-ton civilian spheroid DropShip designed for bulk cargo transport. Its enormous hull provides vast cargo bay capacity, making it one of the largest dedicated freighters ever produced. The drive system provides only modest acceleration, typical of civilian transports that prioritize cargo capacity and fuel efficiency over speed. Defensive armament is minimal, limited to autocannons and medium lasers positioned to deter pirate attacks rather than engage military threats. Armor protection is correspondingly light, sufficient for a civilian vessel operating along established trade routes but wholly inadequate for contested space. The Jumbo's crew complement is substantial, reflecting the vessel's size and the labor-intensive cargo handling systems of its era. Despite its age, the design's fundamental cargo-carrying efficiency kept it competitive for centuries before more modern designs with improved automation and drive technology finally rendered it obsolete. The vessel's most significant limitation beyond its lack of combat capability is its slow transit speed, which increases both fuel consumption and exposure time during approaches to potentially hostile worlds.
text.deployment: The standard Jumbo serves in its baseline bulk cargo transport configuration, carrying massive quantities of raw materials, manufactured goods, and colonial supplies between worlds. These vessels are found exclusively in civilian merchant service, typically operating along established trade routes where escort availability and minimal pirate activity reduce the risk to their lightly armed hulls.
text.battleHistory:
The Jumbo's history stretches back to the earliest days of interstellar colonization, making it one of the most ancient vessel classifications still recognized. The name originally referred generically to any large sub-light cargo ship supporting colonial ventures, predating the invention of the K-F Boom and Docking Collar technology that defined the modern DropShip concept. As standardization took hold, the Jumbo designation came to refer to a specific class of large spheroid freighter optimized for bulk cargo operations.

At its height during the Age of War, the Jumbo served as the backbone of interstellar commerce, its enormous cargo capacity making it indispensable for supplying colonies and supporting the industrial growth of the Great Houses. Multiple manufacturers across the Inner Sphere produced the type, including Krester Ship Construction, Majesty Metals and Manufacturing, Nimakachi Fusion Products, and Shipil Company, ensuring widespread availability.

The Jumbo's decline began in the twenty-eighth century with the introduction of the Mule class, which offered comparable cargo capacity in a more efficient and better-automated hull. As newer designs proliferated, Jumbos were progressively retired from front-line merchant service, with surviving examples relegated to secondary routes and backwater trade runs. The Succession Wars accelerated this decline as battle damage and spare part shortages took their toll on the aging fleet. However, the Jumbo's robust construction meant that scattered examples continued operating well into the thirty-first century, particularly in the Periphery where newer vessels remained scarce.

text.capabilities:
The Aerospace Carrier variant replaces the BattleMech bays with facilities for forty aerospace fighters, making it one of the largest dedicated fighter carriers ever fielded by the SLDF. Six small craft bays supplement the fighter wing, providing utility transport, search and rescue, and shuttle capability. With 1,057.5 tons of cargo capacity, the carrier variant can sustain prolonged aerospace operations with ample stores of ammunition, fuel, and replacement parts for its embarked fighter wing.

The defensive systems, armor, drive, and structural characteristics remain identical to the BattleMech Carrier, with ninety tons of ferro-aluminum armor, 203 double heat sinks, and the same powerful drive system. The Aerospace Carrier was designed to operate as the hub of fighter operations during large-scale fleet engagements, launching and recovering its forty fighters while its own weapons contributed to the defensive screen. The vessel's acceleration advantage over slower transports allowed it to reposition rapidly within a formation to provide fighter cover where needed.
text.deployment: The Aerospace Carrier variant served as a mobile fighter base for SLDF fleet operations, deploying its forty-fighter air wing during major engagements. These carriers proved particularly valuable during the Periphery Uprising, where the ability to project aerospace superiority from a single fast platform gave SLDF commanders decisive advantages in orbital combat. During the Liberation of Terra, Aerospace Carriers were among the first vessels committed to battle, launching their fighters against the Caspar drones before the main transport fleet advanced.
text.battleHistory:
The Lee class DropShip originated from a proposal presented to SLDF Commanding General Aleksandr Kerensky in 2749 by a consortium of three major naval yards in the Terran Hegemony. Kerensky's vision was to reduce the proliferation of military DropShip classes by creating a single design capable of carrying large payloads of SLDF troops into battle faster than anything currently in service. The development process was far from smooth, as political entanglements and boondoggles similar to those that had plagued the earlier Colossus class DropShip threatened to derail the program entirely.

Ironically, Star Lord Richard Cameron's attempts to block the Lee's production proved counterproductive. His opposition galvanized support among the Star League Council members who were increasingly wary of Cameron's erratic governance, and their collective approval pushed the design into production in 2756. The SLDF quickly ordered all four configurations, though the cargo transport variant saw the most limited production run with only three vessels completed before the program's priorities shifted to combat variants.

The Lee first saw major combat during the Periphery Uprising, where its ability to rapidly move large troop formations proved invaluable to the SLDF's suppression campaigns. The class's generous payload capacity allowed commanders to concentrate forces quickly at trouble spots, and the Lee's heavy armament meant it could contribute directly to orbital combat rather than relying entirely on escorts. These early engagements validated Kerensky's original vision of a fast, versatile military transport.

The Amaris Coup and subsequent Liberation of Terra transformed the Lee's role from triumphant to tragic. When the SLDF fought to reclaim the Hegemony, the Space Defense System's Caspar drone fleets proved devastatingly effective against the large, relatively slow transports. The Lee's substantial carrying capacity, once its greatest asset, became a catastrophic liability as each vessel destroyed took an enormous number of troops with it. Losses mounted so rapidly that surviving Lee transports were held in reserve until the final landings on Terra itself, where they deployed in large numbers for the climactic assault.

Few Lee class vessels survived the Liberation of Terra in operational condition, and those that did joined Kerensky's Exodus Fleet on its journey to the deep Periphery. The remaining ships were subsequently lost during the fierce fighting of the Pentagon Civil War, and no examples of the class are known to have survived into the modern era. The Lee stands as both evidence of late Star League engineering ambition and a cautionary example of how concentrated transport capacity can become a strategic vulnerability.

text.capabilities:
The Armor Carrier variant was configured to transport a full battalion of forty heavy combat vehicles alongside a regiment of mechanized infantry comprising twenty-seven platoons. Twenty-eight light vehicle bays provide additional capacity for scout elements and support vehicles, while eight small craft bays facilitate rapid personnel and materiel transfers. Cargo capacity of 1,068.5 tons supports the logistics demands of this large combined-arms force.

The crew complement of 1,356 is by far the largest of any Lee variant, reflecting the substantial number of vehicle crews, infantry personnel, and support staff embarked alongside the vessel's own operating crew. The armor, drive system, weapons array, and structural characteristics are identical to other Lee variants. The Armor Carrier's ability to deliver an entire combined-arms battalion in a single vessel made it invaluable during large-scale planetary assaults, though the concentration of so many troops in a single hull made each loss devastating to the formations depending on these transports.
text.deployment: The Armor Carrier variant was deployed to deliver combined-arms formations during large-scale planetary assaults, carrying heavy vehicle battalions and mechanized infantry regiments as a single integrated force. These vessels saw significant action during the Periphery Uprising, where their ability to land an entire combined-arms force simultaneously proved decisive in several campaigns. The concentration of so many troops in each hull made Armor Carrier losses particularly devastating during the Liberation of Terra, contributing to the decision to hold surviving transports in reserve until absolutely necessary.
text.battleHistory:
The Lee class DropShip originated from a proposal presented to SLDF Commanding General Aleksandr Kerensky in 2749 by a consortium of three major naval yards in the Terran Hegemony. Kerensky's vision was to reduce the proliferation of military DropShip classes by creating a single design capable of carrying large payloads of SLDF troops into battle faster than anything currently in service. The development process was far from smooth, as political entanglements and boondoggles similar to those that had plagued the earlier Colossus class DropShip threatened to derail the program entirely.

Ironically, Star Lord Richard Cameron's attempts to block the Lee's production proved counterproductive. His opposition galvanized support among the Star League Council members who were increasingly wary of Cameron's erratic governance, and their collective approval pushed the design into production in 2756. The SLDF quickly ordered all four configurations, though the cargo transport variant saw the most limited production run with only three vessels completed before the program's priorities shifted to combat variants.

The Lee first saw major combat during the Periphery Uprising, where its ability to rapidly move large troop formations proved invaluable to the SLDF's suppression campaigns. The class's generous payload capacity allowed commanders to concentrate forces quickly at trouble spots, and the Lee's heavy armament meant it could contribute directly to orbital combat rather than relying entirely on escorts. These early engagements validated Kerensky's original vision of a fast, versatile military transport.

The Amaris Coup and subsequent Liberation of Terra transformed the Lee's role from triumphant to tragic. When the SLDF fought to reclaim the Hegemony, the Space Defense System's Caspar drone fleets proved devastatingly effective against the large, relatively slow transports. The Lee's substantial carrying capacity, once its greatest asset, became a catastrophic liability as each vessel destroyed took an enormous number of troops with it. Losses mounted so rapidly that surviving Lee transports were held in reserve until the final landings on Terra itself, where they deployed in large numbers for the climactic assault.

Few Lee class vessels survived the Liberation of Terra in operational condition, and those that did joined Kerensky's Exodus Fleet on its journey to the deep Periphery. The remaining ships were subsequently lost during the fierce fighting of the Pentagon Civil War, and no examples of the class are known to have survived into the modern era. The Lee stands as both a reflection of late Star League engineering ambition and a cautionary example of how concentrated transport capacity can become a strategic vulnerability.

text.capabilities:
The Cargo Carrier variant is the most specialized and rarest configuration of the Lee class, with only three vessels ever completed. Stripping out all troop transport facilities, this variant devotes its entire internal volume to a massive 8,257.5-ton cargo hold, making it one of the fastest high-capacity military cargo runners ever built. The minimal crew of one hundred reflects the simplified internal configuration.

The Cargo Carrier retains the full armor protection, weapons array, and drive system of its combat-oriented sister variants, giving it the ability to defend itself and outrun most threats while carrying critical military supplies. Designed as a blockade runner, the combination of heavy armor, significant defensive firepower, and high acceleration made the Cargo Carrier capable of forcing its way through contested space to deliver vital supplies to besieged garrisons. Its extreme rarity reflected the SLDF's preference for the troop-carrying variants, but the three completed vessels proved their worth during the desperate fighting of the Liberation of Terra.
text.deployment: Only three Cargo Carrier variants were ever produced, and these rare vessels served exclusively as high-speed military supply runners during the final years of the Star League. Their primary mission was delivering critical supplies through contested space lanes, relying on their combination of heavy armor, defensive armament, and high acceleration to survive encounters with enemy forces. All three are believed to have been lost during the fighting on Terra or the subsequent Exodus and Pentagon Civil War.

text.capabilities:
The Pocket WarShip conversion represents the most radical departure from the original Leopard design. The drive system was replaced with a larger and more powerful unit delivering a safe thrust of 2.5 gravities with a maximum of four gravities, nearly doubling the original's acceleration profile. Fifty-four tons of ferro-aluminum armor replaced the standard plating, providing 1,015 points of protection and dramatically increasing survivability in capital-scale engagements. Structural integrity was increased to 12.

The most significant change was the complete removal of all 'Mech and fighter bays, replaced by a single teleoperated Killer Whale capital missile launcher fed by an eleven-missile magazine. This gives the diminutive Leopard hull the ability to threaten WarShips, a capability utterly beyond the original design's scope. The standard weapons suite of the upgraded Leopard was retained for defense against conventional threats. Seventy double heat sinks manage the thermal load, and 58.5 tons of cargo capacity supports limited independent operations. The minimal crew of fifteen reflects the simplified internal configuration.
text.deployment: The Pocket WarShip conversion was developed by the Word of Blake at Irian Naval Systems' Clipperton yards and deployed exclusively by Blakist forces during the Jihad. These converted Leopards served as inexpensive capital-capable combatants, threatening WarShips and other large vessels at a fraction of the cost of purpose-built warships. The type saw extensive action during the Jihad's major naval engagements, where even a handful of Pocket WarShip Leopards could significantly alter the balance of a fleet engagement.

production.manufacturer: Boeing Interstellar|Bowie Industries - Port Sydney|Federated-Boeing Interstellar - Port Simon Shipyards|Irian Technologies - Irian Naval Systems of Clipperton|Taurus Territorial Industries

text.capabilities:
The original Leopard is built around a Star League V84 drive system providing a safe thrust of 1.5 gravities with a maximum of 2.5 gravities. Twenty-nine and a half tons of standard armor cover the angular hull, providing 500 points of protection across all arcs. The weapons array emphasizes energy weapons supplemented by missile batteries, with the nose bay mounting twin PPCs, an LRM-20, and three medium lasers. Each forward-firing wing bay carries a pair of large lasers, an LRM-20, and a medium laser. A dorsal turret mounts twin aft-facing medium lasers, and a single large laser supplements the rear arc firepower. Eighty single heat sinks manage this considerable but well-balanced weapons suite.

The interior houses four individual 'Mech bays, each accessed through large hull doors. The limited internal space means that only mobile repair platforms, small cranes, and industrial exoskeletons can be carried for maintenance, and moving 'Mech components between bays requires using the external doors as the internal passages are too narrow for large parts. Two fighter cubicles sit forward of the 'Mech bays and can be dismantled when no fighters are carried, converting to approximately 300 tons of cargo space or room for six small vehicles, though this space is considered unsuitable for combat units. The standard cargo allocation is 34 tons. Crew quarters are notoriously cramped, with fifteen bunkrooms each housing two people.
text.deployment: The original Leopard served with every Star League member state and has remained the most common lance-sized 'Mech transport throughout the Succession Wars and into the modern era. Its primary mission has always been delivering BattleMech lances for raiding, reconnaissance, and planetary assault operations. The SLDF's AirLance doctrine assigned dedicated Leopards to specific units, creating lasting partnerships between 'Mech formations and their transport crews that persisted through the Succession Wars. Virtually every Successor State, Periphery nation, mercenary command, and pirate band has operated Leopards in some capacity, making it the most widely distributed military DropShip class in history.

production.manufacturer: Federated-Boeing Interstellar - Port Simon Shipyards|Irian Technologies - Irian Naval Systems of Clipperton|Lockheed/CBM Corp.

text.capabilities:
The modernized (3056) Leopard retains the same hull and drive system but incorporates significant improvements to habitability and armament. A more powerful air circulation and filtration system addresses the chronic atmospheric complaints of crews serving on the original model, and while the berths remain cramped, each of the fifteen bunkrooms now features improved facilities. The weapons array was comprehensively upgraded with Star League-era technology, replacing the standard PPCs and large lasers with extended-range models and the medium lasers with pulse variants for improved close-range accuracy.

The three LRM-20 batteries were fitted with Artemis IV fire control systems using the Doombud guidance package, significantly improving missile accuracy against maneuvering targets. Seventy double heat sinks replaced the original eighty singles, providing greatly improved thermal management despite the higher heat generation of the extended-range weapons. Cargo capacity increased to 72 tons. The overall upgrade transforms the Leopard from a capable but aging transport into a vessel competitive with modern designs, while maintaining full backward compatibility with existing maintenance infrastructure.
text.deployment: The upgraded Leopard was produced simultaneously by Irian Naval Systems at Clipperton and Federated-Boeing Interstellar at Galax beginning in 3056, with both manufacturers distributing to their respective state militaries. The controversy over the near-identical designs created diplomatic friction between the Free Worlds League and the Federated Commonwealth but did not slow production. Both versions quickly entered frontline service, with Federated Commonwealth units receiving priority allocation during the escalating tensions of the late 3050s and the subsequent FedCom Civil War.

text.capabilities:
The Leopard CV replaces the standard model's four 'Mech bays with six aerospace fighter cubicles, creating a dedicated small fighter carrier on the same proven hull. The drive system, armor, and weapons array are identical to the original Leopard, with the Star League V84 providing the same thrust profile and eighty single heat sinks managing the thermal load. Twenty-nine and a half tons of standard armor provide 500 points of protection.

The six fighter bays allow the CV to carry a full aerospace squadron, making it the standard small fighter carrier for patrol and escort duties across the Inner Sphere. The carrier version benefited from the development of curved armor plating approximately fifty years after the original Leopard's debut, improving its aerodynamic profile during atmospheric operations. Thirty-four tons of cargo capacity support basic operational needs. The CV has traditionally operated alongside standard Leopards and Fury infantry transports, providing the fighter cover that these lighter-armed vessels require during contested landings.
text.deployment: The Leopard CV entered service in 2581 and quickly became the standard small fighter carrier across the Inner Sphere. Its primary role was providing aerospace escort for transport formations during planetary assault operations, deploying its six-fighter squadron to establish local air superiority. The CV served with every major military power and saw continuous production through the Succession Wars, its simple design and shared components with the standard Leopard ensuring a steady supply of replacement parts.

text.capabilities:
The modernized Leopard CV received upgrades paralleling those applied to the standard model, incorporating recovered Star League technology to improve combat effectiveness. Standard energy weapons were replaced with extended-range and pulse variants, and the LRM batteries received Artemis IV fire control systems for improved missile accuracy. Seventy double heat sinks replaced the original eighty singles, providing superior thermal management with reduced mass.

The six-fighter configuration was retained, and cargo capacity increased to 65.5 tons. The overall improvements mirror those of the standard (3056) Leopard, maintaining the close operational relationship between the two variants. The upgraded CV continues to serve as the primary small fighter carrier for Successor State militaries, providing escort and patrol capabilities that complement the 'Mech transport role of the standard Leopard.
text.deployment: The upgraded Leopard CV entered production in 3054, slightly ahead of the standard model's modernization. Like its 'Mech transport sibling, the upgraded CV was distributed across multiple Successor State militaries, with the Federated Commonwealth and Free Worlds League receiving the bulk of initial production. The improved weapons array and thermal management significantly enhanced the CV's ability to defend itself and its embarked fighters during contested landing operations.

text.overview:
The Lion class DropShip is one of the oldest designs still in active service, originally introduced in 2595 as a Star League combined-arms transport. This 7,300-ton Spheroid was designed from the outset to carry BattleMechs, vehicles, and cargo in a single hull, making it a true multi-role transport capable of deploying balanced ground forces.

Unlike the Clan Union and Overlord vessels, which are essentially new craft sharing a name with Inner Sphere designs, all surviving Lion class vessels are refitted originals constructed during the twenty-seventh century. No new Lions have ever been built, making each surviving example an irreplaceable relic of the Star League era.
text.capabilities:
The original Lion carries two lances of BattleMechs, a company of twelve light vehicles, and over 2,350 tons of cargo. The spheroid hull distributes its weapons across all arcs. The nose mounts four large lasers, four medium lasers, and two LRM-20 racks. Each broadside carries six large lasers, four medium lasers, two LRM-20s, two LRM-15s, and two SRM-6 launchers. The aft arc provides two LRM-15s, two large lasers, two medium lasers, and two SRM-6s. One hundred thirteen single heat sinks manage the thermal load.

The vessel maintains a safe thrust of 3g with a structural integrity rating of 14, and carries 768 points of armor. A crew of 143 operates the vessel and its embarked forces. The Lion's generous cargo capacity allows extended independent operations without resupply.
text.deployment: The original Lion served with the Star League Defense Force as a combined-arms transport throughout the Inner Sphere. Only a handful survived the Succession Wars in Inner Sphere hands, and these rare vessels became prized possessions of whatever military force could maintain them.
text.battleHistory:
The Lion entered service in 2595 as a combined-arms transport for the Star League Defense Force. The design served throughout the Inner Sphere until the Amaris Civil War, when many were destroyed or damaged. The surviving Lions were divided between those that accompanied the Exodus Fleet and the handful that remained in the Inner Sphere, where centuries of Succession War fighting reduced their numbers to a mere fraction of the original production run.

The Clans extensively refitted their Lions to match their revised military organization, expanding the Mech bays from two lances to two Stars and replacing all weapons with advanced Clan technology. An attempt to convert the vehicle bay for battle armor proved unfeasible, and the space was instead configured for an infantry Binary. This compromise relegated the Lion to service with freeborn and dezgra units, who continued to use it in its intended combined-arms role.

When Wolf's Dragoons returned to the Inner Sphere in 3005, they brought several Lion class vessels, which they expected would be inconspicuous. They did not realize that only a handful of Lions remained in Successor State fleets, and their presence immediately aroused suspicion. The Dragoons stripped most advanced technology from their Lions before arriving and restricted them to carrying eight BattleMechs to avoid further scrutiny. After the Fourth Succession War, the Dragoons adopted the five-unit Clan organization openly, and following the Battle of Luthien in 3052, most of their Lions are believed to have been returned to full Clan specifications.

The KR-61C performs the same logistical function within Clan Occupation Zones, serving Jade Falcon and Ghost Bear transportation networks. text.overview:
The Mammoth class is the largest DropShip capable of landing on a planet, serving as the backbone of bulk cargo transportation across the Inner Sphere since its introduction in 2658. Designed by Krester's Ship Construction as a massive spheroid freighter, the Mammoth dwarfs most other cargo carriers at 52,000 tons, hauling nearly 38,000 tons of goods across five enormous cargo decks. Few vessels of this scale are independently owned, with most belonging to large megacorporations or Successor State governments. Several states have modified Mammoths to serve as diatomic-hydrogen fuel tankers, while others act as fleet refueling vessels for extended operations.

The high operating and maintenance costs associated with a vessel of this immense size restrict the Mammoth's use to major trade routes between well-developed worlds, making it an uncommon but unmistakable sight wherever interstellar commerce flows at scale.
text.capabilities:
The original Mammoth features five massive cargo decks, each holding slightly more than 7,000 tons of goods for a combined capacity approaching 38,000 tons. Two 300-ton cargo lifts link all five decks, enabling efficient redistribution of cargo throughout the vessel. The lowest deck contains a pair of enormous doors for planetary loading and unloading operations, while the second deck mounts four airlocks for orbital cargo transfer. Four small craft bays provide auxiliary transport and shuttle capability for the vessel's crew and cargo operations.

The Mammoth's most distinctive feature is its drive system. Rather than a single central engine, four separate Bally Tech Super X40 drive units are mounted externally on the hull, each connected via explosive bolts. These engine modules can be jettisoned or shut down in an emergency, though they must be ejected in pairs to avoid catastrophic thrust imbalance. Each drive pod contains a small internal control room for independent operation, though without attitude control or navigation systems, standalone use is impractical. This configuration frees additional internal volume for cargo at the expense of ironically cramped crew quarters, with thirty double-occupancy rooms for most of the crew and eight single rooms for senior officers. The vessel carries 21.5 tons of standard armor and 262 single heat sinks to support its defensive weapons.
text.deployment: The original Mammoth entered service with the Star League's largest commercial shipping concerns and military logistics commands, plying the major trade routes between the most prosperous worlds of the Inner Sphere. The Star League Defense Force operated a significant fleet for strategic supply operations, while several Successor States employed modified versions as diatomic-hydrogen fuel tankers to support extended fleet operations far from established refueling infrastructure. The vessel's enormous size restricted its use to only the wealthiest operators, ensuring that the sight of a Mammoth in orbit signaled the presence of serious commercial or military investment.
text.battleHistory:
Krester's Ship Construction introduced the Mammoth class in 2658 during the height of the Star League era, when expanding interstellar commerce demanded bulk cargo carriers of unprecedented capacity. The design proved immediately successful, with its massive cargo capacity and innovative drive system attracting contracts from the largest trading concerns and military logistics commands in the Inner Sphere. The original design was eventually sold to foreign customers, ensuring that production continued at multiple facilities even after Krester's Ship Construction itself ceased operations.

When the Star League collapsed, the Mammoth's sophisticated engineering became both a blessing and a curse. The vessel's sheer cargo capacity remained irreplaceable for bulk transport operations, but the complexity of its quad-engine drive system and advanced components made maintenance increasingly difficult as the Succession Wars eroded the Inner Sphere's technological base. Spare parts grew scarce, and operators frequently cannibalized damaged vessels to keep others flying, steadily reducing the total number in service throughout the First and Second Succession Wars.

By the late Succession Wars era, the surviving Mammoth fleet had stabilized as manufacturers adapted production methods to work within available technological capabilities. A revised model introduced around 2808 incorporated adjustments to accommodate the declining industrial base while preserving the vessel's essential cargo capacity. Production was maintained at facilities operated by Federated-Boeing Interstellar, Kathil Shipworks, Tengo Aerospace, and others across the Inner Sphere, ensuring that the Mammoth remained available to those organizations wealthy enough to operate one.

Throughout all eras, the Mammoth's role has remained consistent: moving massive quantities of goods between major trade worlds. Modified variants serving as fuel tankers have proved equally valuable, providing critical refueling capability for military fleets operating far from established supply lines. The vessel's enduring presence on every major trade route across the Inner Sphere stands as evidence of the soundness of its original design.

text.overview:
The Manatee holds a singular place in military history as the first DropShip converted to carry BattleMechs. Originally a compact 1,900-ton Spheroid cargo vessel, the design was selected by the Terran Hegemony Naval Department as the most promising hull for adaptation into a BattleMech transport when the newly invented war machines required a means of reaching the battlefield.

While the Manatee's tenure as a BattleMech carrier proved brief, its basic form inspired the creation of all dedicated BattleMech transports that followed, most especially the Star League era Confederate class. The original cargo variant continued in far more mundane but enduring service, remaining in production for centuries despite its historical significance being forever linked to its short-lived military role.
text.deployment: The standard Manatee represents the historic military conversion that became the first BattleMech-carrying DropShip. Converted from Bordello Military Goods' existing cargo hull at the direction of the Terran Hegemony Naval Department, the military Manatee replaced its cargo bays with BattleMech restraint systems capable of securing a lance of the newly developed war machines. First deployed against the Fourth Avalon Hussars on Kentares in 2449, the Manatee proved the concept of orbital BattleMech deployment, though its light armor and modest armament made it vulnerable to concentrated ground fire. While quickly superseded by purpose-built carriers, the military Manatee established the fundamental principles of BattleMech transport that would guide all subsequent designs.

These vessels operate on secondary trade routes and in logistical support roles where their small crew requirements and low operating costs make them economically viable.

text.capabilities:
The Ngake variant stands as a radical conversion into a pocket WarShip configuration. Fighter bays and all standard weapons are removed to accommodate four sub-capital laser class-1 weapons in the nose, giving the vessel anti-WarShip capability. Close defense is provided by fourteen Large X-Pulse Lasers distributed across all arcs, while fourteen Laser Anti-Missile Systems provide comprehensive missile defense coverage. Heat sink capacity increases dramatically to 140 double sinks to support the energy-intensive weapons suite.

Cargo capacity drops to 297 tons with the fighter bays removed entirely. The crew complement increases slightly to twenty-seven. Thrust performance, armor protection, and structural integrity remain identical to the base Merlin, making the Ngake variant equally maneuverable while carrying capital-grade weapons.
text.deployment: The Ngake is a unique vessel captured from the Word of Blake during the Jihad and refitted by the Principality of Regulus. First spotted undergoing conversion at the Ngake system, this one-of-a-kind pocket WarShip demonstrated the viability of mounting sub-capital weapons on the Merlin hull and served as the proof-of-concept for the subsequent R1 production variant.

text.capabilities:
The R1 is the production version of the Ngake pocket WarShip, intended for orbital fire support of ground troops. The variant retains the four nose-mounted sub-capital laser class-1 weapons and fourteen Large X-Pulse Lasers but reduces Laser AMS coverage to ten systems. A single aerospace fighter bay is restored, providing limited organic fighter support that the Ngake lacked.

Fuel capacity is slightly reduced compared to the Ngake variant, and cargo space drops to 149 tons. The crew complement increases to twenty-eight. Heat management remains robust with 140 double heat sinks. The non-standard quirk designation reflects the vessel's hand-built nature, as the Principality of Regulus must acquire new or salvaged base Merlins and convert them individually rather than producing purpose-built R1 hulls.
text.deployment: The R1 entered limited production for the Principality of Regulus beginning in 3082, intended to provide orbital fire support for ground operations. Production remains constrained by the need to acquire standard Merlins for hand conversion, keeping the number of operational R1 variants small within Regulan naval forces.

text.deployment: The Mówáng serves as a personal transport for nobility, senior officials, and wealthy private owners throughout the Capellan Confederation and neighboring states. Most examples operate as intra-system couriers, moving passengers between planetary surfaces, orbital facilities, and jump points. A smaller number serve as discreet transports for valuables or sensitive cargo where the owner wishes to avoid formal shipping channels. The open manufacturing license means the craft can be found in virtually any Capellan duchy or warren, and examples are common enough in neighboring realms that they rarely attract attention during routine transit.

The Clandestine variant operates exclusively as a covert assault transport for Word of Blake operatives during the Jihad period. Outwardly indistinguishable from a standard Mówáng, the craft approaches its objective concealed within the traffic of a civilian DropShip or JumpShip, then separates for its attack run. The Angel ECM suite is activated before approach to jam communications and degrade tracking, followed by bombing of the target site. Two Level Is of battle armor are then deployed for ground operations, and the craft stands by to extract the troops or continue suppressing first responders with additional bomb runs. The Internal Bomb Bay is the primary stand-off weapon, used both before and after troop deployment.

text.capabilities: The Armored Pocket WarShip variant combines the full AR-10 missile armament and fighter bays of the standard Pocket WarShip with the reinforced 616-point armor package, providing maximum survivability for sustained engagements. Cargo capacity is reduced slightly to 371 tons compared to the Q-Ship, and the crew complement is marginally smaller at 45. In all other respects this configuration mirrors the standard Pocket WarShip, with four AR-10 launchers, six aerospace fighter bays, and 160 double heat sinks. The Armored variant represents the most combat-capable Mule conversion, intended for direct naval engagements where deception is unnecessary and sustained firepower exchange is expected.
text.deployment: The Armored Pocket WarShip served alongside the standard and Q-Ship variants in Word of Blake naval formations, typically assigned to engagements where open battle was expected rather than ambush. Its reinforced armor allowed it to sustain fire from hostile DropShips and aerospace fighters while delivering capital missile strikes, making it the most survivable of the three Jihad-era Mule combat conversions.

text.capabilities: The Star League-era Pocket WarShip variant strips the Mule of its cargo capacity to mount a fearsome array of capital missile systems. Three White Shark and three Barracuda launchers replace the upper cargo bays, supplied by thirty-nine reloads stored in armored magazines. Six aerospace fighter bays provide a screening force for the converted freighter, with only 413 tons of residual cargo space remaining. Armor protection more than doubles to 616 points, and 160 double heat sinks replace the original singles to manage the thermal demands of the capital weapons. The crew complement nearly doubles to 54 to handle the complex weapons systems and fighter operations.
text.deployment: The Star League-era Pocket WarShip saw limited deployment with the SLDF's naval auxiliary forces, providing capital missile capability in theaters where dedicated WarShip support was unavailable. Few of these conversions survived the Succession Wars intact, though the concept would be revived centuries later by the Word of Blake. The variant demonstrated that even a civilian hull could be transformed into a credible naval combatant with sufficient armament and armor upgrades.

text.overview: The Oo-Suzumebachi, whose name translates to "giant hornet" from Japanese, is a purpose-built assault craft developed by the Draconis Combine following the Second Combine-Dominion War. Designed to deliver battle armor directly into hot landing zones, the first prototype cleared trials at Dover in 3117. Production models quickly became the preferred transport of small-unit battlesuit commanders across the DCMS, earning the nickname "Ooze" from the crews who fly them.
text.capabilities:
The Oo-Suzumebachi takes a straightforward approach to its mission, prioritizing protection and firepower over technological sophistication. Its most notable feature is its heavy Ferro-Aluminum armor, with the majority of that protection concentrated on the nose and sides to shield troops during assault approaches. Six anti-missile systems across its wing sections provide layered defense against missile fire, allowing the craft to push through defended airspace that would stop more lightly armored transports.

A powerful main weapon is fitted to clear the landing zone ahead of disembarking troops, and the design handles both atmospheric and space flight, giving commanders flexibility in how and where it is deployed. Its brute-force philosophy means the Ooze will never outperform a dedicated aerospace fighter in a straight engagement, and it carries no pretense of being a high-technology platform. Crew accommodations are basic, with steerage-class sleeping quarters reflecting the craft's utilitarian focus.
text.deployment: The Oo-Suzumebachi serves the Draconis Combine's special operations and assault infantry forces as a dedicated battle armor transport. It is typically assigned to small-unit battlesuit commanders requiring a rugged, well-armed craft capable of delivering troops under fire. The design pairs effectively with conventional aerospace escort and operates from both DropShip bays and forward ground bases.
text.battleHistory:
The Oo-Suzumebachi was developed in the years following the Second Combine-Dominion War, as the DCMS reconsidered how best to deliver battle armor in contested environments. The first prototype flew at Dover in 3117, and the design entered production the following year.

The craft saw early operational use during the Draconis Reach campaigns of 3139, where several Oozes supported Ryuken-go operations against Davion installations. At Wapakoneta, four craft fought through fixed defenses to prevent a Davion counterattack from striking a Dragoon column. Using their anti-missile systems to suppress defending LRM batteries, the Oozes delivered troops directly onto fortified positions and held the bridgehead long enough to secure the Dragoon withdrawal.

By 3144, the design had become a recognized tool of the DCMS's assault infantry doctrine. During the conquest of Cimeron against the Fifth Robinson Strikers, elements of the Twenty-second New Samarkand Regulars used a small force of Oozes to insert battlesuit infantry onto an enemy air base while the regiment's fighters and DropShips staged a diversion. The operation eliminated the LCT's aerospace assets and forced the Fifth to withdraw off-world.

text.overview:
The Outpost is a seven-thousand-ton Spheroid assault DropShip designed from the ground up by Clan Hell's Horses to carry a truly mixed military force of BattleMechs, armor, infantry, aerospace fighters, and battle armor. Commissioned in 3061, the design addressed the Clan's long-standing dissatisfaction with the patchwork conversions of existing Union-C and Overlord-C transports that had been individually modified for combined-arms use.

Falling between the Union and Overlord classes in size, the Outpost can attain nearly double the acceleration of either vessel, allowing it to outmaneuver or outrun the most common DropShips encountered during planetary assault missions. Protected by heavier armor than even the Overlord-C and mounting formidable weaponry, the design gives its operators a powerful advantage during contested landings.
text.capabilities:
The 3070 refit replaces the Streak SRM launchers with five Hyper-Assault Gauss 30 autocannons distributed across all arcs, dramatically increasing the vessel's anti-armor and anti-DropShip firepower. The nose mounts a HAG/30 alongside four ER large lasers, six medium pulse lasers, and three anti-missile systems. Each side carries two HAG/30s along with six ER large lasers and eight medium pulse lasers, with four anti-missile systems. The aft arc mounts a HAG/30 alongside two ER large lasers, four medium pulse lasers, and two anti-missile systems. One hundred and seventy double heat sinks handle the thermal load.

The transport configuration shifts to accommodate two ProtoMech Points and ten battle armor Points alongside the five Mech and ten vehicle bays. Cargo capacity increases to 1,814 tons, and crew complement rises to 236 to service the expanded troop contingent.
text.deployment: The 3070 refit expanded the Outpost's combined-arms capability to include ProtoMech elements, reflecting Clan Hell's Horses' growing incorporation of these assets into their force structure. These upgraded vessels continued to serve as the primary combat transports for Horse combined-arms formations, with the heavier weapons load providing improved fire support during contested landings.
text.battleHistory:
The Outpost class was born from Clan Hell's Horses' recognition in the early 3060s that their naval transport fleet was an unsatisfactory collection of individually converted DropShips. Rather than continue modifying existing designs, saKhan Tanya DeLaurel commissioned a complete ground-up design in 3061, requesting a vessel faster and sturdier than the standard Mech carriers used throughout Clan space, capable of serving as an effective mobile command and coordination center during major operations.

The Clan's aerospace engineers used the rare Fortress class DropShip as a baseline, upgrading nearly every positive aspect of that venerable design while adding improvements of their own. The resulting Outpost class entered service in 3063, and its ability to carry a balanced combined-arms force in a single hull quickly proved its worth during operations where the Horses' integrated doctrine demanded seamless cooperation between Mech, armor, and infantry elements.

Subsequent variants expanded the design's capabilities. A 3070 refit incorporated hyper-assault Gauss weapons and facilities for ProtoMech and expanded battle armor contingents, while a Defender configuration introduced capital missile systems and dedicated aerospace fighter capacity for a fleet defense role.
