text.overview:
The Overlord class DropShip is one of the most recognizable and widely-produced military transport vessels in the Inner Sphere. First launched in 2762, this 9,700-ton Spheroid design quickly became the standard by which all other regiment-level Mek carriers would be judged. Produced by numerous shipyards across both the Inner Sphere and Clan space, the Overlord has served continuously for over three centuries, evidence of the fundamental soundness of its original design. Its distinctive teardrop profile and massive bay doors have become iconic symbols of military power projection throughout the BattleTech universe. Few designs have achieved such universal adoption across virtually every major military force in known space.

The sheer number of Overlords in service has made the class a common sight in virtually every major conflict since the fall of the Star League, and its continued production ensures it will remain so for the foreseeable future.
text.capabilities:
The original Overlord carries a full battalion of thirty-six BattleMeks supported by a half-dozen aerospace fighters, making it one of the most potent single-vessel combat transports of its era. Its 132.5 tons of dedicated cargo space provides sufficient room for spare parts and ammunition resupply, while 120 single heat sinks manage the thermal load from its considerable weapons array. The vessel mounts PPCs and autocannons across all firing arcs, with LRM-20 racks providing long-range fire support and a mix of large and medium lasers covering close defense. The nose arc concentrates the heaviest firepower with paired PPCs, AC/20s, AC/5s, and LRM-20 racks, giving the Overlord devastating forward firepower during orbital insertion.

With a crew complement of 141 and first-class quarters for command staff, the Overlord provides comfortable long-duration transport for its embarked forces. Six bay doors allow rapid deployment of its Mek complement, a critical advantage during contested landings. The Spheroid hull design provides excellent stability during planetary descent and a broad base for ground operations. Ferro-aluminum armor provides solid protection across all arcs, with the heaviest coverage on the nose to absorb incoming fire during the vulnerable descent phase. Rear-mounted weapons on both broadsides ensure that no approach vector is left undefended.
text.deployment: The original Overlord entered service with the Star League Defense Force in 2762 and was adopted by virtually every major military power following the Amaris Civil War and the Succession Wars. Its combination of Mek carrying capacity, fighter support, and defensive armament made it the standard regimental transport for centuries. Every Great House military operated significant numbers, and the design remained in continuous production at multiple facilities throughout the Inner Sphere. The Overlord's ubiquity made it the default expectation for any serious planetary assault force, and military planners across the Inner Sphere built their force projection doctrine around its capabilities.
text.battleHistory:
The Overlord class DropShip traces its origins to the height of the Star League era, when the Star League Defense Force recognized the need for a standardized heavy Mek transport capable of deploying a full battalion in a single vessel. Previous designs had forced commanders to split their forces across multiple smaller transports, complicating coordination during contested landings. The Overlord was designed from the ground up to solve this problem, with bay capacity for thirty-six BattleMeks and integral aerospace fighter support.

Entering service in 2762, the Overlord quickly proved its worth during the Amaris Civil War, where SLDF forces used the design extensively during the liberation of Terra. The ability to land an entire battalion in a single drop, supported by its own fighter screen and considerable defensive armament, gave the Overlord a decisive advantage in contested planetary assaults. When Aleksandr Kerensky led the Exodus, hundreds of Overlords accompanied the SLDF fleet into the unknown.

The Succession Wars that followed the Star League's collapse only increased the Overlord's importance. As JumpShip numbers dwindled and each transit became more precious, the ability to move a full battalion on a single docking collar became even more valuable. Production continued at reduced rates throughout the Succession Wars, and captured Overlords were among the most prized spoils of war. The Clans independently developed the Overlord C variant, scaling the hull up to 11,600 tons to carry forty-five Meks organized in the Clan Trinary structure.

The Clan Invasion of 3049 prompted the first major refit of the Inner Sphere Overlord in centuries. The 3056 variant replaced aging autocannons with Gauss rifles and upgraded energy weapons to their ER equivalents, dramatically improving the design's ability to survive contested drops against Clan-grade opposition. The Word of Blake Jihad later spawned the A3 and A3A pocket WarShip conversions, mounting capital-grade weapons on the proven Overlord hull.

Today the Overlord remains in widespread service across virtually every major military force in the Inner Sphere and Clan space. Its longevity is a reflection of the soundness of the original Star League design, and continued production ensures the class will remain the backbone of military DropShip fleets for decades to come.

The 3056 refit modernizes the Overlord in response to the Clan Invasion, replacing its aging autocannon armament with Gauss rifles across all firing arcs. ER PPCs replace standard models, and LRM-20 racks receive Artemis IV fire control. ER large lasers supplement the primary batteries. Structural integrity increases from 18 to 20 and total armor coverage rises slightly to 816 points. The Gauss rifles provide devastating long-range striking power without the ammunition explosion risk that made autocannon magazines a critical vulnerability on earlier models.

The refit maintains the standard thirty-six Mek bays and six aerospace fighter slots, though cargo capacity drops to just 99 tons as the heavier Gauss rifle installations consume available space. Despite the reduced cargo, the dramatically improved firepower makes this variant far more capable of surviving contested orbital insertions against Clan-grade opposition. The combination of extended-range energy weapons and Gauss rifles gives the 3056 Overlord the ability to engage targets at ranges where older models would be completely outmatched by Clan naval assets. The improved structural integrity also enhances survivability against the punishing weapons fire encountered during Clan engagements.
text.deployment: The 3056 refit emerged as the Inner Sphere's response to the technological shock of the Clan Invasion. Upgrading existing Overlord hulls with Gauss rifles, ER weapons, and Artemis fire control brought the venerable design closer to parity with Clan opposition. The refit saw widespread adoption among the major powers of the Inner Sphere during the 3050s and 3060s, with every Great House converting significant portions of their existing Overlord fleets to the new standard as quickly as production capacity for Gauss rifles and extended-range energy weapons allowed.

text.deployment: The standard Pentagon represents the primary production variant that served throughout the Star League era. Upgraded from the original Mk I with improved heat management, extended-range energy weapons, and modern fire control systems, this variant became the definitive anti-fighter escort vessel of the SLDF navy. Its exceptional thrust-to-mass ratio made it one of the fastest DropShips of its era, capable of matching the acceleration profiles of most fighter escorts while providing concentrated firepower against incoming aerospace threats. The standard Pentagon served with distinction during the Periphery uprisings and the Amaris Civil War before being thought extinct following the Exodus.

text.capabilities: The 2751 Royal upgrade was available exclusively to Terran Hegemony units. This variant replaces the standard PPCs of the regular Star League version with ER PPCs, extending engagement range significantly while retaining the same Gauss rifles, ER large lasers, and Artemis IV-equipped LRM-20 launchers. Double heat sinks replace the single models, dramatically improving sustained fire capability. Armor protection, drive performance, and structural integrity remain identical to the standard Star League variant. Cargo capacity holds at 573 tons.
text.deployment: The Royal Pentagon served exclusively with Terran Hegemony units, operating alongside the elite formations of the SLDF's most prestigious commands. These vessels shared the same fate as other Royal equipment, with surviving examples taken by General Kerensky into exile following the fall of the Star League.

The original Pentagon Mk I served with the Terran Hegemony Navy from the mid-twenty-sixth century, operating as an anti-fighter escort attached to Congress-class Frigates and other capital warships. These vessels were among the most active combat DropShips in the SLDF fleet, regularly engaging pirates, Periphery raiders, and hostile aerospace formations during convoy escort duties.

production.manufacturer: Majesty Metals and Manufacturing

text.deployment: The standard Princess Luxury Liner represents the original passenger configuration that set new standards for interstellar travel when it entered service in 2657. Carrying up to two hundred passengers across three classes of accommodation, the standard variant features amenities including a full swimming pool, wine cellars, a simulated garden environment on the Earth Deck, and private balcony suites for ultra-luxury guests. Minimal armament reflects the vessel's purely civilian role, with defensive weapons limited to a single large laser and a handful of medium lasers and machine guns. The standard Princess found its primary market among the nobility and wealthy merchant classes of the Star League, with regular service routes connecting the great capitals of the Inner Sphere.

production.manufacturer: Refit - Majesty Metals and Manufacturing

text.deployment: The cargo refit became the most common configuration for surviving Princess vessels outside the Magistracy of Canopus. The Succession Wars made luxury passenger service economically unviable for most operators, and conversion to a bulk freighter allowed these large vessels to remain productive. Cargo-configured Princess vessels served as civilian transports along major trade routes across the Inner Sphere, their impressive cargo capacity making them valuable assets despite their age and maintenance requirements.

text.capabilities:
The Seeker's Quad RanTech 720 fusion drive system accounts for almost a third of the vessel's mass and is the key to its performance. The drive consists of four small fusion reactors, each independently operated and shielded. Engineers can work on a single reactor without shutting down the entire system, and the Seeker can operate on two reactors for extended periods or a single reactor in emergencies, providing exceptional redundancy for long-range independent operations.

Energy weapons dominate the arsenal. Each side mounts a PPC, a large laser, two medium lasers, and an LRM-10 launcher. The aft arc carries a large laser and two medium lasers. One hundred and one single heat sinks manage the thermal output. The reconfigurable main bays normally carry forty light vehicles and nine infantry platoons, with 491 tons of cargo space holding spare parts, food, and water for four months of independent operations. Crew and passenger quarters are luxurious by military standards, and an extensive medical facility handles most field emergencies.
text.deployment: The original Seeker has served in virtually every Inner Sphere military since 2815, typically assigned to scout battalions and reconnaissance commands requiring independent deep-penetration capability. Multiple manufacturers across the Inner Sphere ensured broad availability, and the design's four-month endurance made it the preferred transport for extended scouting missions where resupply was uncertain.

production.manufacturer: Salvatore Inc.|Semier Data Tron|Tengo Aerospace

text.capabilities:
The 3054 upgrade replaces the standard PPCs with ER PPCs and the large lasers with ER large lasers across all arcs, significantly extending engagement range. Each LRM-10 launcher receives an Artemis IV fire control system for improved missile accuracy. The aft arc similarly upgrades to an ER large laser with two medium lasers. These weapon modifications are relatively modest, preserving the Seeker's proven reliability while extending the effective reach of its defensive armament.

More extensive changes were made to the transport bays and support systems. A MASH (Mobile Army Surgical Hospital) unit enhances the vessel's already capable medical facilities, reflecting the upgraded variant's continued focus on extended independent operations deep in hostile territory. Transport capacity remains at forty light vehicles and nine infantry platoons with 489 tons of cargo space. The Quad RanTech 720 drive system and one hundred and one single heat sinks are unchanged from the original design.
text.deployment: The upgraded Seeker was jointly developed by Semier Data Tron and Salvatore Inc. for the Federated Commonwealth in 3054 and saw rapid adoption across the Federated Commonwealth's scout and reconnaissance commands. The extended-range weapons and improved medical facilities enhanced the vessel's already proven capability for independent long-duration operations in contested space.

text.capabilities:
Powered by an Entech 200c fusion engine, the ST-46 achieves a safe acceleration of 2G and a maximum of 3G. Its aerodyne profile reduces fuel consumption during atmospheric descent, an advantage over spheroid craft of similar mass. With only 5 tons of fuel, the ST-46's range is limited to short inter-orbital and planetary transit; the explicit gap that prompted development of the companion KR-61. Unlike that design, the ST-46 carries no sleeping or food preparation accommodations.

The craft carries 18.5 tons of standard armor, substantially more protection than the KR-61's 6 tons, reflecting its more frequent atmospheric and docking operations where minor collisions and landing stress are routine. The ST-46 is entirely unarmed. A significant structural limitation is the lack of internal access between the forward passenger section and the aft cargo hold: crew must exit the craft to reach the starboard cargo hatch, though ducting does connect the cargo section to the engineering bay. The design also requires a prepared ferrocrete runway for landing, making it unsuitable for operations on undeveloped worlds where only rough terrain is available.

Passenger capacity is eight, accessed through the cockpit or the vessel's single airlock. The 12-ton cargo hold offers nearly five times the payload of the KR-61, reinforcing the ST-46's role as a bulk short-range workhorse rather than a long-haul passenger craft.
text.deployment: The ST-46 serves as the standard short-range shuttle aboard JumpShips, WarShips, space stations, and large transport vessels across every major faction. It handles routine cargo transfers, crew transport, and passenger runs that do not justify detaching a full DropShip. Unlike the KR-61, it is optimized for high-frequency short hops rather than long runs to distant jump points.

text.overview: The Taihou is an assault DropShip produced by Hinsdale Elec for the Draconis Combine as part of the nation's post-Jihad naval rebuilding program. Entering service in 3079, the Taihou was designed through a collaboration between Hinsdale Elec, personnel from the Midway Warship Yard, and electronic systems specialists from the Nirasaki Computers Collective. The result was a compact but devastating assault vessel capable of engaging targets up to and including WarShips, providing the Combine with a domestically produced capital-capable combat vessel to help replace the naval assets depleted during the Jihad.
text.capabilities: The Taihou is a 12,000-ton military aerodyne assault DropShip mounting a fearsome array of weaponry. Its primary anti-ship armament consists of four Heavy Sub-Capital Cannons capable of threatening WarShip-class targets, supplemented by twelve Heavy PPCs and MRM 40 launchers equipped with Apollo fire control systems for engaging conventional targets. A Screen Launcher and anti-missile systems provide defensive countermeasures against incoming ordnance. One hundred fifteen tons of Heavy Ferro-Aluminum armor gives the Taihou exceptional survivability for a vessel of its size, allowing it to absorb sustained fire while closing to effective engagement range. The design incorporates a Nirasaki Naval C3 System, which coordinates fire between squadrons of similarly equipped vessels, dramatically enhancing the effectiveness of Taihou flotillas operating in concert. The drive system provides adequate acceleration for fleet operations. The vessel also carries a complement of battle armor marines for boarding operations. The Taihou's combination of sub-capital weapons, heavy armor, and networked fire control makes it a genuine threat to larger vessels, though its relatively compact hull limits the amount of punishment it can absorb in prolonged fleet engagements.
text.deployment: The standard Taihou Assault DropShip serves in its baseline anti-ship configuration, providing capital-grade firepower for Draconis Combine naval task forces. These vessels typically operate in small squadrons linked by networked fire control systems, coordinating their attacks to maximize effectiveness against larger targets.
text.battleHistory:
The Taihou was born from the Draconis Combine's desperate need to rebuild its naval combat capability in the aftermath of the Jihad. The Word of Blake's systematic destruction of Combine WarShips and shipyard facilities had left the DCMS critically short of capital-grade combat vessels, a deficiency that threatened the Combine's ability to defend its borders against rival powers that retained their own naval assets.

The development program brought together expertise from across the Combine's remaining industrial base. Hinsdale Elec provided the primary shipyard and construction capability, while personnel from the Midway Warship Yard contributed their experience with naval combat vessel design. The Nirasaki Computers Collective developed the advanced networked fire control system that would become one of the Taihou's most distinctive features, allowing squadrons of assault DropShips to coordinate their fire with unprecedented precision.

The first Taihou entered service in 3079, providing the Combine with a domestically produced vessel capable of engaging WarShip-class targets at a fraction of the cost of a true capital ship. The class proved its worth in subsequent fleet exercises and border deployments, where networked Taihou squadrons demonstrated the ability to concentrate devastating firepower on targets far larger than any individual ship. The design has remained in production, gradually rebuilding the Combine's ability to project naval power along its frontiers.

production.manufacturer: Vandenberg Mechanized Industries

text.overview: The Tigress Close Patrol Craft was developed by Vandenberg Mechanized Industries shortly after the fall of the Star League, entering service in 2790 as a dedicated system defense platform for the Taurian Concordat. Originally conceived as a DropShip and WarShip escort in the mold of earlier Star League designs, shifting strategic priorities redirected the Tigress toward local patrol duties as the Concordat focused on defending the densely fortified Hyades Cluster against Successor State aggression. The craft's modest size, self-sufficient fuel supply for patrols of up to a week, and manageable crew requirements made it an ideal platform for operations in the asteroid fields and approach corridors of the Cluster. Neither the fastest nor the most heavily armed craft of its type, the Tigress trades raw performance for the reliability, endurance, and affordability that a Periphery power requires from a frontline patrol asset.
text.capabilities:
The Tigress is built around a nose-mounted PPC and a fifteen-tube Long Range Missile launcher, giving it effective firepower at both energy and ballistic ranges without the complexity of more varied weapon combinations. The LRM rack carries thirty-two salvos, sufficient for an extended patrol without resupply. For close-range engagements, four medium lasers split between the two wing sections provide respectable short-range firepower, though the Tigress is not optimized for brawling against heavier craft at close quarters.

The craft's fusion engine gives it maximum thrust of 3g, adequate for intercept work in the constrained geometry of system patrol operations. Fifteen tons of fuel support patrols of just over eight days at continuous thrust, a practical endurance for asteroid field and jump point picket duties. A seven-ton cargo bay allows the Tigress to carry limited stores for extended independent operations. The design is solid rather than exceptional, reflecting the Concordat's preference for maintainability and cost of ownership over peak performance. The Tigress's primary vulnerability is the absence of any aft-arc weaponry, leaving it exposed to threats that successfully close behind the craft's forward firing arc.
text.deployment: The Tigress Close Patrol Craft serves almost exclusively with the Taurian Concordat Aerospace Forces, assigned primarily to defensive patrol duties in the Hyades Cluster. Craft are typically deployed in small groups covering asteroid belts, jump point approaches, and inner system corridors of inhabited worlds. The seven-ton cargo bay allows Tigress patrols to carry limited supplies for extended independent operations, reducing resupply frequency in the Concordat's resource-constrained Periphery environment. A small number of Tigress craft have reached the hands of Periphery operators and independent actors over the centuries, though the design's Taurian-specific support infrastructure has limited its spread beyond Concordat space.
text.battleHistory:
Vandenberg Mechanized Industries began designing the Tigress as the Aquarius and Lyonesse were disappearing from production. The escort small craft role those designs had built was contracting across the Inner Sphere, absorbed by heavier aerospace fighters and newer DropShip classes. Vandenberg's designers looked at that contraction and reached a different conclusion than the major powers had. For the Taurian Concordat, with its densely fortified Hyades Cluster and its permanent concern about Federated Suns aggression, the need for affordable, self-sufficient patrol craft had not diminished. It had grown. The Tigress, introduced in 2790, carried that lineage forward into the Periphery while the Inner Sphere abandoned it.

The original design intent was closer to the Aquarius than what the Tigress became. Vandenberg planned a DropShip and WarShip escort operating in the Star League tradition. Shifting strategic priorities during development redirected the craft toward system patrol duties, covering the asteroid fields and approach corridors of the Hyades Cluster rather than riding alongside capital ships. The PPC and LRM armament suited this role well, engaging threats at range before they could threaten defended installations or passing convoys. For nearly three centuries the Tigress served that function with little change, operated by minimal crews on week-long patrols through some of the most heavily mined and monitored space in the Periphery.

The design earned wider recognition during the Jihad. In 3076, Taurian gunships participated in a nuclear strike raid on the New Syrtis Shipyards, a suicidal deployment that crippled the facility and underscored both the Concordat's willingness to commit its patrol craft offensively and the depth of political tensions that had been building with the Federated Suns. Vandenberg continued production through the Dark Age and into the ilClan era, making the Tigress one of the longest-lived small craft designs of the Periphery, an unbroken line of service that outlasted the Inner Sphere powers that had abandoned the escort role entirely.

text.overview:
The Titan class DropShip stands as one of the largest dedicated aerospace fighter carriers ever constructed, purpose-built to transport and support the fighter complement of an entire battalion. Introduced in 2647 during the height of the Star League, this massive aerodyne carrier was designed with fighter pilots firmly in mind, offering relatively luxurious crew quarters, expansive flight decks, and an extensive tactical command station for the vessel's aerospace commander. A single Titan carries enough fighters to overwhelm the aerospace defenses of most jump points or planetary garrisons.

The vessel's heavy armor and powerful weapons array minimize the inherent risks of concentrating so many fighters aboard a single hull, though the indiscriminate warfare of the Succession Wars ultimately proved that even the Titan's formidable defenses could not guarantee survival. No Inner Sphere examples survived past the First Succession War, though the class continues to serve with distinction among the Clan toumans.
text.capabilities:
The original Titan carries eighteen aerospace fighters across three separate flight decks, each housing six fighters and capable of independent operations. This distributed arrangement ensures that damage to one flight deck does not cripple the entire fighter wing, while the three-deck layout provides flexibility in launching coordinated strikes from multiple vectors simultaneously. Nearly 2,887 tons of cargo capacity supports extended operations with ample stores of spare parts, munitions, and supplies for the embarked fighter wing. Four small craft bays provide utility transport and search-and-rescue capability.

The vessel mounts 78 tons of standard armor and a weapons array centered on autocannons, PPCs, and laser batteries distributed across all firing arcs, with 195 single heat sinks managing the thermal load. The large bridge contains a dedicated tactical post for the aerospace commander, who directs fighter launch and recovery operations and provides a real-time tactical information feed to each pilot during combat. The GM 750-A12 drive system delivers a safe thrust of 2.5 gravities, providing good maneuverability for a vessel of this size. Pilot and crew quarters are among the finest aboard any DropShip, with single-occupancy cabins for all personnel and shared bathroom facilities for each Point of pilots. Senior officer cabins include dedicated computer terminals for administrative work.
text.deployment: The original Titan served with the Star League Defense Force as a premier fighter carrier, typically assigned to escort WarShip task forces or operate independently as system patrol craft. The SLDF deployed Titans to contested systems where their massive fighter complements could establish aerospace superiority quickly and decisively. The class was considered too large and valuable for attachment to individual ground units, instead operating at the fleet level under naval command authority. All Inner Sphere Titans were lost during the First Succession War, with the last destroyed by Draconis Combine fighters at Cholame.
text.battleHistory:
Di Tron Heavy Industries launched the first Titan class carrier in 2647 to meet the Star League Defense Force's requirement for a high-capacity aerospace fighter transport capable of independent operations. The design proved highly successful, with its combination of fighter capacity, heavy armament, and crew amenities earning praise from both pilots and naval command staff. The SLDF deployed Titans as WarShip escorts and independent system patrol craft, with the vessel's fighter complement providing a formidable force projection capability that could dominate the aerospace environment around any contested world.

The Succession Wars proved catastrophic for the Inner Sphere's Titan fleet. The concentration of so many valuable fighters aboard a single hull made each Titan a priority target, and the increasingly desperate warfare of the era left no room for the restraint that might have preserved these irreplaceable carriers. Draconis Combine fighters destroyed the last Inner Sphere Titan during the series of battles at Cholame during the First Succession War, ending the class's service in the Inner Sphere after less than a century.

The Titan endured among the Clans, however, as a number of vessels accompanied the Exodus fleet into the Deep Periphery. These carriers continued to serve in the various Clan toumans, receiving a significant refit beginning in 2953 that expanded their fighter capacity from the original eighteen to a full Trinary of thirty OmniFighters. Each of the three flight decks was upgraded to service ten fighters and launch them from dual access doors, dramatically improving sortie rates during combat operations.

The Clan Titan's weapons array was also substantially enhanced beyond even the formidable original specification, exceeding the firepower of dedicated assault DropShips such as the Achilles class. Following the Jihad, Clan Snow Raven converted several Titans into Monitor-class Pocket WarShips to protect their new holdings in the Outworlds Alliance after the loss of several WarShips during the conflict. These heavily modified vessels traded fighter capacity for capital-grade weaponry and enhanced defensive systems, ensuring the Titan's continued relevance well into the post-Jihad era.

production.manufacturer: BBP Industries|Rashpur-Owens Inc.

text.capabilities:
The original Triumph carries a full battalion of forty-five heavy combat vehicles across three massive bays located on the vessel's two lowest decks. A pair of oversized doors on the craft's flanks provides excellent access for rapid offloading, while eight additional light vehicle slots and four infantry bays round out its troop transport capability. The aft section of the lowest deck houses the transit drive, landing gear, one main bay, and two supplementary cargo bays totaling over 750 tons of additional capacity. Though these auxiliary bays have restricted floor space limiting them to roughly four vehicles each, they prove ideal for storing BattleMeks or Mek cubicles when needed.

Defensively, the Triumph mounts a modest weapons array centered on autocannons, PPCs, and laser batteries spread across all firing arcs, supplemented by LRM racks for long-range deterrence. With 112 single heat sinks managing thermal load and only 36.5 tons of standard armor, the design prioritizes cargo capacity over combat survivability. A crew of over 530 personnel operates and maintains the vessel, reflecting the extensive support requirements of its embarked vehicle battalion. The Delano 1070 drive system provides a safe thrust of 1.5 gravities, adequate for a vessel of this size though insufficient for evasive maneuvering under fire.
text.deployment: The original Triumph served as the primary aerodyne vehicle carrier for the Star League Defense Force from 2593 onward, and continued in that role with all five Successor States following the Star League's dissolution. Every Great House operated significant numbers throughout the Succession Wars, relying on the Triumph to deliver armored formations to contested worlds across the Inner Sphere. Production was maintained at facilities including the Rashpur-Owens shipyards on Capella and Aldis Industries plants, though output declined steadily as the conflicts ground on. The design's vulnerability in hostile landing zones led most commanders to deploy Triumphs only with substantial fighter and assault DropShip escort, a doctrine that became standard practice across all Successor State militaries.

production.manufacturer: BBP Industries

text.capabilities:
The 3057 redesign by BBP Industries serves as a comprehensive overhaul rather than a simple refit, reducing total displacement to 6,000 tons while incorporating recovered Star League technology throughout. The redesigned interior replaces the original single massive ramp with a pair of narrower ramps providing simultaneous access to upper and lower vehicle bays, allowing crews to reorganize cargo during flight. Twenty-four heavy vehicle slots and twelve light vehicle positions are supplemented by four Mek cubicles, giving the new Triumph the ability to transport a Mek lance alongside two companies of armor.

The weapons array receives significant upgrades, replacing the nose-mounted autocannon with a Gauss rifle and trading standard energy weapons for extended-range and pulse variants. Artemis IV fire control systems improve the accuracy of all LRM launchers, significantly enhancing the vessel's ability to defend itself during approach and landing operations. Unlike many lostech refits of the era that amounted to little more than weapon swaps, the BBP redesign fundamentally improved the Triumph's operational flexibility while reducing its logistical footprint. Cargo capacity drops to 242 tons, a trade-off accepted in exchange for the added Mek transport capability and improved combat effectiveness.
text.deployment: The BBP Industries redesign entered service with the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery in 3057, produced at the Luthien shipyards. Its ability to carry both Meks and vehicles in a single hull made it attractive to combined-arms regiments operating along the Clan border, where tactical flexibility was paramount. The upgraded weaponry and improved bay access significantly enhanced survivability during contested landings that would have been extremely hazardous for the older model. Limited production capacity meant relatively few of the new-model Triumphs reached front-line units during the initial production run, though those that did were highly valued by their crews for the vastly improved cargo handling and combat capability.

production.manufacturer: Field Refit|Taurus Territorial Industries|Vandenberg Mechanized Industries

text.overview:
The Trojan is a 3,200-ton Spheroid blockade runner derived from the unarmed Danais class cargo vessel, originally converted within the Taurian Concordat beginning around 2745. These conversions added weapons and defensive systems to the civilian hull while accepting a modest reduction in cargo and passenger capacity. The Trojan designation applies broadly to armed Danais conversions rather than a single standardized configuration, meaning individual vessels can vary significantly in their specific weapons loadout.

Designed for smuggling and self-defense rather than frontline combat, the Trojan fills a niche between unarmed merchant vessels and purpose-built military transports. The design proved remarkably enduring, with converted Danais vessels continuing to serve in the blockade runner and armed transport role for centuries after the first examples appeared.
text.capabilities:
The typical Trojan blockade runner configuration mounts a weapons suite oriented toward deterrence and breakout engagements rather than sustained combat. The nose carries two LRM-20 racks and two medium lasers, providing moderate long-range punch. Each broadside mounts two LRM-20 racks, a large laser, and four medium lasers, giving the vessel respectable broadside firepower for its size. The aft arc is defended by two medium lasers to discourage pursuit.

Eighty-four single heat sinks manage the thermal output from this energy-heavy arsenal. The vessel carries 396 points of armor, adequate for surviving brief engagements but insufficient for prolonged combat against dedicated military vessels. Two small craft bays provide utility transport and scouting capability. The primary cargo hold retains 1,533 tons of capacity, reduced from the unmodified Danais but still substantial for a vessel in the blockade runner role. A crew of thirty operates the ship, maintaining the small complement typical of civilian-derived vessels.
text.deployment: Trojan blockade runners operated across the Inner Sphere in the hands of independent merchants, smugglers, and minor state navies from the late Star League era onward. The Taurian Concordat fielded the earliest examples, but Trojan conversions spread widely during the Succession Wars as the demand for armed transports grew. During the Jihad, these vessels saw renewed prominence as HPG blackout runners, maintaining vital supply lines between isolated worlds.
text.battleHistory:
The first Trojan conversions appeared in the Taurian Concordat around 2745, where unarmed Danais cargo vessels were modified with weapons for smuggling operations and self-defense along contested borders. The conversions were relatively straightforward, requiring only the installation of weapons bays and fire control systems in space previously allocated to cargo or passenger accommodations.

After the fall of the Star League, the escalating violence of the Succession Wars made armed conversion increasingly attractive to Danais operators across the Inner Sphere. Many more vessels received the Trojan treatment as the perils of interstellar travel grew. The design remained active for centuries, adapting to changing threats. During the Jihad, Trojan blockade runners proved particularly valuable in maintaining lines of communication between worlds cut off when the HPG grid was disrupted. Some vessels were used to smuggle cargo in and out of the Word of Blake's Protectorate, running Blakist blockades at considerable risk. Given the Trojan's nature as a field conversion rather than a factory-built design, no two vessels are necessarily identical in their specific armament and configuration.

production.manufacturer: Markesan Aeronautics

text.deployment: The standard Vampire represents the original Star League Defense Force configuration that entered production in 2715. One of the smallest military DropShips ever fielded, it was designed specifically to deliver jump infantry platoons via ventral drop hatches during high-speed atmospheric passes. The standard variant carries minimal defensive armament, relying instead on its fighter-equivalent acceleration and small sensor cross-section to survive transit through contested airspace. Its drive system, while providing exceptional performance for the hull's mass, was notoriously maintenance-intensive with a comparatively short operational lifespan between overhauls.

The Vampire II entered production in 3070, created specifically for the AFFS Rabid Foxes special operations unit for battle armor infantry deployment. These vessels operate in the same high-speed insertion role as the original Vampire, substituting armored infantry for jump troops while maintaining the design's signature ability to be mistaken for aerospace fighters during approach runs.

text.capabilities:
The Vampire III returns to the original 400-ton displacement while incorporating modern battle armor delivery capability. Four Battle Armor bays and sixteen tons of cargo replace the original's jump infantry compartments. The weapons suite shifts to a missile and laser combination: the nose mounts two ER medium lasers and an Artemis-equipped SRM-6, each wing carries an Artemis-equipped LRM-20 and two ER medium lasers, and the aft arc mounts two ER medium lasers.

Protected by 460 points of heavy ferro-aluminum armor, the Vampire III trades the raw firepower of the Vampire II for restored speed, matching the original's safe thrust of six. Twenty-three double heat sinks easily handle the modest thermal output of the missile and laser armament. A crew of fifty-nine operates the vessel. The structural integrity of eleven matches the original design, maintaining the Vampire's characteristic resilience during high-speed combat insertions.
text.deployment: The Vampire III entered service in 3094 as a more affordable alternative to the heavier Vampire II, returning to the original's 400-ton displacement while retaining battle armor delivery capability. These vessels have seen service with AFFS special operations forces, continuing the Vampire lineage's tradition of high-speed covert insertion missions.

text.capabilities:
The Vengeance mounts armament distributed across all arcs, though its weapons serve primarily as self-defense rather than primary offensive firepower. The nose concentrates a large laser with two medium lasers, while each wing forward arc mirrors this configuration. The heavier armament sits in the wing rear arcs, with each side mounting a PPC, two LRM-20 racks, an AC/5, a large laser, and four medium lasers. The aft arc carries an AC/5, an LRM-10, and two medium lasers. One hundred forty-eight single heat sinks manage the thermal load from this considerable arsenal.

The vessel's true combat power lies in its forty aerospace fighter bays, organized into two twenty-fighter wings with separate launch and recovery facilities. Three small craft bays provide utility transport and search-and-rescue capability. The Warrior-ATP drive system provides 2g safe thrust despite the vessel's 11,400-ton mass. The flat, boxy hull design that accommodates the fighter bays prevents atmospheric operations, confining the Vengeance to space-based deployments. The crew of one hundred seventeen includes six dedicated gunners, though the ship's own weapons remain secondary to its role as a fighter platform.
text.deployment: The original Vengeance served as the backbone of Star League Defense Force carrier operations from its introduction in 2682. Following the League's collapse, all five Successor States scrambled to secure Vengeance carriers, recognizing the decisive advantage a forty-fighter wing could provide in system-defense and offensive operations. The Federated Suns and Lyran Commonwealth maintained the largest Vengeance fleets during the Succession Wars, leveraging their greater industrial capacity to keep aging carriers operational. These vessels typically anchored defensive positions at critical jump points or served as the centerpiece of offensive task forces during major campaigns.

production.manufacturer: Kallon Weapon Industries|Salvatore Inc./Kallon Weapon Industries|Tomori Trans Industrial

text.capabilities:
The (3056) upgrade significantly enhanced the Vengeance's defensive armament while preserving its forty-fighter complement. The nose received a Gauss rifle alongside ER large lasers, dramatically improving engagement range and alpha strike potential. Each wing's PPCs were replaced with ER models, and all four LRM-20 racks gained Artemis IV fire control systems for improved accuracy against maneuvering targets. The wing and nose large lasers were upgraded to extended-range variants throughout. The aft retained its AC/5 and LRM-10, with the latter also receiving Artemis IV.

These upgrades freed tonnage for an additional 227 tons of cargo capacity, raising the total from 218 to 446 tons. The 148 single heat sinks remained unchanged despite the increased energy weapon output, as the Gauss rifle generates minimal heat. The Warrior-ATP drive system and armor protection remained identical to the base design, and the crew decreased slightly to one hundred fifteen with the elimination of one gunner position.
text.deployment: The upgraded Vengeance entered service in 3056, with refitted vessels distributed primarily among the Federated Commonwealth's naval forces. The improved engagement range made these carriers more capable of defending themselves while deploying their fighter wings, reducing reliance on dedicated escort vessels. The variant saw action during the FedCom Civil War and subsequent conflicts, with both Lyran and Davion factions fielding upgraded Vengeance carriers in opposing fleets.
